jobs.title: Sales Manager
jobs.description:
The Sales Manager ensures that company sales goals are met or exceeded including achieving all key business metrics while following the California Closets policies and procedures. This role ensures that the Design Consultants are delivering on the California Closets standards of excellence with each and every customer. The Sales Manager also collaborates with the GM and Operations Team to make sure that the process flow is being followed and results in delivering a high standard of customer service at all touchpoints.

Job Highlights:

• We're located on 807 S Kings Hwy, Fort Pierce, FL 34945, USA
• The schedule for this position is Monday - Friday from 8am-5:00pm with night and weekend flexibility needed.
• The salary for this position is $80k-$100k + Bonus (based on experience).

What We Offer:

California Closets has both company-owned and franchise locations. This location is company-owned, therefore earns the following benefits:

• Health insurance – Medical, Dental, and Vision
• PTO days and paid holidays
• 401K retirement plan with company match
• Grow your career with us – many promotional opportunities available
• Generous company discounts
• Referral bonuses
• Some locations provide cell phone stipends

Franchises are independently owned and operated and may offer different benefits.

Duties and Responsibilities:

• Collaborate with GM to hire and retain top talent based on the budgeted number of Design Consultants.
• Manage a team of Design Consultants ensuring all company revenue goals and key performance indicators are met or exceeded. Ensure the Design Team has the appropriate mix of company leads and personal marketing plan leads.
• Performance management of underperformers while following guidelines to improve results including detailed documentation.
• Collaborate with head office operations team on process flow and identify opportunities for improvement.
• Conduct monthly goal setting and reviews with all team members.
• Work closely with the GM on a variety of initiatives including the creation of sales contests and incentive programs, a sustainable charitable strategy, and develop a sustainable trade business strategy.
• Schedule and facilitate monthly Sales Meetings including coordination with guest speakers and head office personnel.
• Analyze sales data and develop a strategy with GM to address areas of opportunity.
• Ensure correct usage of CRM (dashboard) including quality of data entry, statuses, etc.
• Review feedback through 5 Star and follow up on all negative responses with the customer and or Design Consultant, communicate findings to GM.

• 3 -5 years as a Sales Consultant or in a sales management role preferred.
• Industry experience is a plus.
• Proven sales coach and mentor.
• Strong conflict resolution skills.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
• Familiarity with data analysis and reporting.
• Exceptional customer experience skills.
• Experience with design fundamentals preferred.
• Experience with CAD is a plus.
• Experience leading commission-only sales team is highly preferred.

Find us on Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram

We are an equal opportunity employer. We E-Verify.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Lead Consultant, Geologist
jobs.description:
Hybrid-based position in our Syracuse office.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your excellence in an inclusive, collaborative, and empowering community? Are you excited about joining a company that strives to make a difference – for its employees, clients, and society? Are you motivated by creating sustainable change that benefits society and nature?

If this sounds like you, or you’re curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Environment & Health team and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

Your new role

We invite you to bring your environmental consulting experience into play as you support provide technical and project leadership for environmental investigation and remediation projects in the New York area. In this position, the selected candidate will lead and support multidisciplinary teams working closely with Professional Engineers (PEs), Professional Geologists (PGs), Licensed Site Remediation Professionals (LSRPs) and other technical specialists.

As a senior member of the team, you will apply your technical expertise and professional judgment to guide site investigation and remediation strategies, oversee field programs and data evaluation, prepare and review technical deliverables, and support regulatory and client communications. You will also provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior and mid-level staff while helping ensure projects are completed efficiently, safely, and in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

The position provides opportunities to work on a diverse range of projects involving, geologic and environmental investigations, conceptual site model development, remedial strategy and design, data evaluation and modelling, regulatory compliance and technical reporting.

Your key tasks and responsibilities for this role will be:

• Lead and oversee geologic and site investigations, including Remedial Investigations, Feasibility Studies, Remedial Designs, Remedial Actions, and post-remediation OM&M plan and oversee various drilling methodologies and investigation techniques, including monitoring well installations, packer testing, groundwater sampling, and vapor intrusion investigations.
• Oversee and review detailed and accurate field and project documentation; manage and successfully track field and project activities related to scope, schedule, and budget.
• Serve as a key technical point of contact for clients and project stakeholders, communicating investigation findings, technical recommendations, project status, and emerging issues; participate in client meetings and work collaboratively with LSRP and technical leads to develop practical solutions that meet project and client objectives.
• Coordinate the development and finalization through final submission of technical documents, including regulatory reports, work plans, and biennial remedial action protectiveness submittals, pursuant to regulatory requirements; independently develop scopes of work and budgetary cost estimates and support initial project setup, invoicing, and project closeout.
• Proactively communicate change management needs during project execution; provide technical guidance and mentorship to early-career and mid-level Geological Scientists and contribute to the development of team capabilities and technical best practices.

About you

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Geological Science, Environmental Science, or related field, with 5+ years of relevant experience.
• Possession, eligibility, or demonstrated progress toward obtaining, a PG license and/or LSRP.
• At a minimum, 40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification and up-to-date 8-hour refresher; additional OSHA health and safety training and certifications are a plus.
• Strong working knowledge of federal New York environmental and site remediation regulations, with demonstrated experience applying regulatory requirements to investigation and remediation projects.
• Demonstrated experience coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, managing technical tasks, and communicating technical findings and recommendations to clients, regulators, and other project stakeholders; strong proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

What we can offer you

• Meaningful, high-impact work
• Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
• Competitive compensation and benefits
• Professional development and leadership opportunities
• A collaborative and inclusive culture
• The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $81,515 – $101,891 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do.  Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application with your up-to-date CV. We invite diversity in all its forms and encourage applicants from all groups to apply.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.title: da Vinci Specialist - St Petersburg
jobs.description:
*Please note: Candidates must live within or be willing to relocate to the St Petersburg, FL Area to perform the duties of this role.

Primary Function of Position

The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.

The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the da Vinci Clinical Sales Representative .

Essential Job Duties

Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)

• Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
• Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
• Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
• Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.

Clinical & Technical Support

• Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.

• Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
• Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
• Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.

• Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
• Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
• Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
• Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).

Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)

• Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
• Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
• Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
• Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
• Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.

Escalation & Customer Issue Management

• Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
• Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
• Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).

Market & Clinical Insights

• Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners. Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
• Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
• Assist in clinical trial support when required.
• Assist in field action activities when necessary.

Required Skills and Experience

• Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
• Clinical experience is preferred.
• Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
• Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
• Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
• Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
• Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
• Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
• Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
• Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
• Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
• Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
• Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.

Required Education and Training

• Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
• Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.

Working Conditions

• Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

We provide market-competitive compensation packages, inclusive of base pay + CIP, benefits, and equity. The target pay rate for this position is:

Base salary region 1: $115,500

Base salary region 2: $105,000

For any Intuitive role subject to export controls, final offers are contingent upon obtaining an approved export license and/or an executed TCP prior to the prospective employee’s start date, which may or may not be flexible, and within a timeframe that does not unreasonably impede the hiring need. jobs.title: SAR Quality assurance specialist
jobs.description:
As a Quality Assurance Specialist with a focus on SAR Reporting at Wise, you are responsible for providing expert, objective assurance on the quality and effectiveness of our operational processes and controls. Your core function is to ensure risks are identified, assessed and mitigated in line with policy requirements, and to identify weaknesses, assess risk materiality and report outcomes. You will apply your risk expertise and critical thinking to conduct holistic and detailed reviews in line with agreed methodologies and KPIs, and make recommendations to drive continuous improvement. This role plays an integral part in helping Wise achieve its mission of Money WIthout Borders, through effective and value-add assurance.

This is a role for specialist who has had experience with external suspicious activity reporting, regulatory compliance and FIUs.

Activities performed on the job

• Conduct holistic, risk-based reviews using test scripts and scorecards to assess risk outcomes, compliance with global and regional policies, relevant guidance and risk appetite.
• Assess risk, materiality and root causes for each finding, providing clear and robust reasons aligned to policy compliance and/or risk mitigation.
• Participate in calibration exercises to share findings, best practice and ensure consistent, correct decisions are made across the team.
• Clearly communicate outcomes to stakeholders covering key risks, issues, root causes, and recommendations, maintaining robust records and audit trails.
• Analyse, assess and communicate emerging themes and trends, recommending opportunities for continuous improvement.
• When assigned, scope, plan, and execute root cause analysis or targeted investigations.
• Contributes to team collaboration and knowledge sharing to enhance team capabilities.
• Take a proactive approach to consistently achieving individual and team targets (KPIs, SLAs), demonstrating a strong commitment to both quality and speed. Meet deadlines, optimise processing times and take full ownership and accountability to deliver results.
• Perform additional tasks as assigned by your lead, demonstrating adaptability and a proactive approach. This includes actively participating in meetings, training, and internal events to support broader team and company objectives.
• Embody and uphold Wise’s values in daily interactions.

Required Skills:

• Professional experience: 2+ years of experience in QA related to BSA/AML or experience in AML Investigations or SAR Reporting
• Fluent in English (written and verbal skills) with the ability to clearly articulate your thoughts and recommendations.
• Self-Development: Takes ownership for personal development, including commitment to develop expertise through industry and trend analysis, regulatory insights, and emerging risk typologies.

Functional Skills:

• Quality Assurance methodology: Good understanding of Quality Assurance methodologies and frameworks, including testing procedures, scoring criteria and root cause analysis. Applies consistent standards across all reviews.
• Risk and Compliance expertise relevant to SAR Reporting, including the ability to identify and assess risks, interpret and apply policy requirements and guidance, and a good understanding of the regulatory environment applicable to the function.
• Analytical Skills: Efficient at reviewing and investigating customer files, identifying missing information, issues, trends and root causes, using AI and data as appropriate.
• Systems and Tools: Competent using case management systems, dashboards, AI tools to support case working and analysis. Understands automation, AI, and is comfortable working with evolving tools and technologies to enhance ways of working.

Behavioural  Skills:

• Critical thinking: Ability to critically assess information, demonstrate attention to detail, challenge assumptions, dig deeper where required, ask the right questions and connect data across different sources to make informed and risk-based decisions, explaining your rationale to ensure our QA outcomes can withstand audit and regulatory scrutiny.
• Risk management: Uses facts, data, policy and risk frameworks to support conclusions and assess risk materiality ensuring decisions can be justified.
• Documentation and communication skills: Clear, constructive and concise written and verbal skills, with ability to explain risks and issues in simple terms in a constructive and actionable manner.

• Adaptability: Able to keep up with evolving requirements and ongoing changes impacting QA team, policy, guidance, processes and systems. Open to feedback and continuous improvement.

Effective expectations and KPIs

• Dynamic KPIs and expectations ensure that the metrics used to evaluate performance remain relevant and aligned with the goals and circumstances of the team and the individual. This flexibility helps both the organisation and employees adapt to change and continuously improve.
• The KPIs and effective expectations are designed to measure effectiveness, productivity, and overall contribution to team and company objectives, while also setting clear behavioural standards for the assigned role. KPIs and expectations are dynamic and will be shared with you for your role and team.

For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.

We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.

Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.

If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

Keep up to date with life at Wise by following us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor - Construction Management
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is seeking an experienced Senior Cost Manager and/or Quantity Surveyor to join our Phoenix team and support a diverse portfolio of large-scale construction projects, including data centers, commercial real estate, high-tech, and semiconductor manufacturing facilities for key clients throughout the Phoenix market and across the broader region.

In this role, you will serve as a key day-to-day client interface, ensuring client objectives are achieved through the delivery of value-added cost management services across all phases of the project lifecycle.

To be successful, you must possess strong communication skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing environment. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, driven, and capable of working both independently and collaboratively within high-performing project teams. This is a significant opportunity to provide leadership and direction while promoting the purpose, values, and vision of Turner & Townsend and delivering best-in-class cost management solutions for some of the region's most complex and high-profile projects.

Responsibilities

• Estimating and negotiating change orders throughout the construction lifecycle.
• Provide estimate and cost planning to include producing and presenting the final cost plan.
• Review and participate with the design services team and general contractor in the development of cost estimates.
• Reconcile changes and assist the general contractor to ensure that their data is accurate.
• Communicate or meet with the general contractor and owner of project manager to gather status information to prepare a cost estimate update.
• Prepare written comments to the general contractor’s submissions, including the executive summary.
• Coordinate all sources of cost information for cost discussions and suppliers direct from NPA, subs, quantities from A/Es.
• Inform and drive engineering priorities based on cost impact.
• Work proactively with minimal supervision to resolve scheduling issues.
• Manage cost checks and carry out valuations on larger projects. Complete timely, accurate cost checking and valuation processes.
• Participate effectively with post-contract cost variances and the change of control processes.
• Manage Cost impact / contingency management and commitment tracking logs.
• Prepare funding data presentations and coordinate VE sessions with stakeholders.
• Developing cost plans and estimates through the design phase, delivering updated cost plans at appropriate design milestones.
• Providing commercial input to design optioneering and input into value engineering exercises.
• Reviewing contractor and subcontractor pricing and leading negotiations on behalf of the client to drive fair contract prices.
• Performing quantity surveying, cost controls, and change management activities throughout the project lifecycle.
• Ensuring that post-contract cost variances and change control processes are managed effectively.
• Ensuring that cost auditing and valuation work is managed effectively and that a robust process for cost validation is in place.
• Carrying out the production of monthly cost reports for presentation to the client.
• Ensuring that final accounts are negotiated and agreed upon in a timely manner.
• Compiling built cost estimate records for benchmarking purposes.
• Identify, coach and mentor talent to realize their potential and celebrate the success of others.
• Display excellence in leadership and service delivery on commissions in line with the conditions of appointment.
• Financial Management - Utilize internal software to track ongoing margin levels and monthly fee/resource forecasts for each commission and financial reports.
• Implement and maintain the use of internal Business Management Systems and company delivery methodologies and tools in the office to ensure consistent delivery of best practice for Clients and the company.
• Be a role model that drives a one business culture that achieves great outcomes by striking the right balance for our people, clients, stakeholders, and society.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, cost management, quantity surveying, engineering or field related to construction.
• Minimum 5-7 years of relevant experience working in a cost management role in the construction industry.
• RICS accredited or working towards it is preferred.
• Experience of leading cost management on medium or large sized construction projects of medium to high complexity.
• Construction consultancy experience is strongly preferred.
• Good knowledge of construction industry technical matters, such as different procurement routes, value management, and value engineering.
• Excellent communication skills.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our clients' needs.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.

Please find out more about us at www.turnerandtownsend.com/

Turner & Townsend does not accept any speculative or unsolicited CV’s that have been sent to our internal recruitment team or hiring managers from agencies outside of our preferred supplier list or that have not followed due process. Any speculative or unsolicited CV’s will be treated as a direct application.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Control Manager – Data Center Construction
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend are looking for an experienced Senior Cost Manager to act as the key day-to-day client interface, delivering cost management services across a large-scale data center program.

This role will have a strong emphasis on change management, cost control, and commercial governance, ensuring that all project changes are effectively evaluated, managed, and communicated throughout the construction lifecycle within a fast-paced, high-volume program environment.

To be successful in this role you must have strong communication skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing role. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, detail-oriented, and experienced in managing complex change processes across multiple stakeholders. In this position, you will provide leadership and direction, embedding and promoting the purpose, values, and vision of Turner & Townsend.

Responsibilities:

• Lead and manage change management processes across the program, ensuring all changes are properly identified, evaluated, documented, and approved.
• Review, evaluate, and negotiate change orders throughout the construction lifecycle, ensuring commercial alignment and cost transparency.
• Maintain and manage change logs, contingency tracking, and commitment registers, providing clear visibility into cost impacts.
• Establish and enforce change control procedures and governance frameworks across multiple projects within the campus.
• Provide detailed cost analysis and recommendations to support client decision-making on change events.
• Support dispute avoidance and resolution through strong commercial oversight and documentation of changes.
• Provide cost planning and estimating, including producing and presenting final cost plans.
• Review and participate with the design team and general contractor in developing cost estimates.
• Reconcile changes and validate contractor cost data to ensure accuracy and completeness.
• Communicate with the general contractor and project team to gather updates and support cost reporting.
• Prepare written comments on contractor submissions, including executive summaries.
• Coordinate cost inputs from subcontractors, suppliers, and design teams.
• Inform and help drive construction priorities based on cost and change impact.
• Work proactively to resolve cost, scope, and scheduling conflicts.
• Manage cost checks and carry out valuations on complex projects.
• Lead post-contract cost variance analysis and ensure adherence to change control processes.
• Prepare funding updates and support value engineering sessions, particularly in response to change drivers.
• Develop cost plans through design and provide updates at key milestones.
• Review contractor pricing and support negotiations to ensure fair and commercially sound outcomes.
• Ensure cost auditing, validation, and reporting processes are consistently applied.
• Produce monthly cost reports with clear visibility into change activity, risks, and forecast impacts.
• Support final account closeout, ensuring all changes are fully agreed and reconciled.
• Maintain cost benchmarking data and program records to support future forecasting and decision-making.
• Mentor team members and promote best practices in change management and cost control.
• Manage financial tracking, forecasting, and reporting for commissions.
• Support internal systems, governance processes, and company delivery methodologies.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Regular onsite presence is required.
• Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, or related field.
• 5–7+ years of cost management or project controls experience on medium‑ to large‑scale construction programs.
• Mission‑critical, industrial, or large campus‑scale experience preferred.
• Consultancy experience strongly preferred.
• Strong understanding of civil, structural, and MEP construction.
• Advanced knowledge of budgeting, financial reporting, cost‑control systems, and Earned Value Management (EVM).
• Proven experience managing full change‑management processes on major construction programs.
• Strong cost‑focused project controls background, including forecasting and variance analysis.
• Ability to interpret schedules and assess cost impacts across phases and trades.
• Expertise in procurement strategy and commercial contract management.
• RICS accreditation (or progress toward certification) is advantageous.
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder‑management skills.
• Strong analytical abilities and attention to detail.
• Proficiency with industry‑standard cost management tools and Microsoft Office.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor – Data Center Construction
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend are looking for an experienced Senior Cost Manager to act as the key day-to-day client interface, delivering cost management services across a large-scale data center program.

This role will have a strong emphasis on change management, cost control, and commercial governance, ensuring that all project changes are effectively evaluated, managed, and communicated throughout the construction lifecycle within a fast-paced, high-volume program environment.

To be successful in this role you must have strong communication skills and be comfortable operating in a client-facing role. The ideal candidate will be self-motivated, detail-oriented, and experienced in managing complex change processes across multiple stakeholders. In this position, you will provide leadership and direction, embedding and promoting the purpose, values, and vision of Turner & Townsend.

Responsibilities:

• Lead and manage change management processes across the program, ensuring all changes are properly identified, evaluated, documented, and approved.
• Review, evaluate, and negotiate change orders throughout the construction lifecycle, ensuring commercial alignment and cost transparency.
• Maintain and manage change logs, contingency tracking, and commitment registers, providing clear visibility into cost impacts.
• Establish and enforce change control procedures and governance frameworks across multiple projects within the campus.
• Provide detailed cost analysis and recommendations to support client decision-making on change events.
• Support dispute avoidance and resolution through strong commercial oversight and documentation of changes.
• Provide cost planning and estimating, including producing and presenting final cost plans.
• Review and participate with the design team and general contractor in developing cost estimates.
• Reconcile changes and validate contractor cost data to ensure accuracy and completeness.
• Communicate with the general contractor and project team to gather updates and support cost reporting.
• Prepare written comments on contractor submissions, including executive summaries.
• Coordinate cost inputs from subcontractors, suppliers, and design teams.
• Inform and help drive construction priorities based on cost and change impact.
• Work proactively to resolve cost, scope, and scheduling conflicts.
• Manage cost checks and carry out valuations on complex projects.
• Lead post-contract cost variance analysis and ensure adherence to change control processes.
• Prepare funding updates and support value engineering sessions, particularly in response to change drivers.
• Develop cost plans through design and provide updates at key milestones.
• Review contractor pricing and support negotiations to ensure fair and commercially sound outcomes.
• Ensure cost auditing, validation, and reporting processes are consistently applied.
• Produce monthly cost reports with clear visibility into change activity, risks, and forecast impacts.
• Support final account closeout, ensuring all changes are fully agreed and reconciled.
• Maintain cost benchmarking data and program records to support future forecasting and decision-making.
• Mentor team members and promote best practices in change management and cost control.
• Manage financial tracking, forecasting, and reporting for commissions.
• Support internal systems, governance processes, and company delivery methodologies.
• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Regular onsite presence is required.
• Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, or related field.
• 5–7+ years of cost management or project controls experience on medium‑ to large‑scale construction programs.
• Mission‑critical, industrial, or large campus‑scale experience preferred.
• Consultancy experience strongly preferred.
• Strong understanding of civil, structural, and MEP construction.
• Advanced knowledge of budgeting, financial reporting, cost‑control systems, and Earned Value Management (EVM).
• Proven experience managing full change‑management processes on major construction programs.
• Strong cost‑focused project controls background, including forecasting and variance analysis.
• Ability to interpret schedules and assess cost impacts across phases and trades.
• Expertise in procurement strategy and commercial contract management.
• RICS accreditation (or progress toward certification) is advantageous.
• Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder‑management skills.
• Strong analytical abilities and attention to detail.
• Proficiency with industry‑standard cost management tools and Microsoft Office.

*On-site presence and requirements may change depending on our client's needs.

Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.

We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.

jobs.description:

jobs.title: Project Management Lead (Contract)
jobs.description:
Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced contract Project Management Lead to own the full lifecycle of client engagements across annual reports, proxy statements, ESG/ sustainability reports, brand identity, and website projects. This person will serve as the primary day-to-day client contact and internal driver, managing scope, schedule, budget, and cross-functional teams from SOW through final delivery.

This is a hands-on delivery role. The right candidate is equally comfortable running a weekly client huddle with senior executives, building a production schedule against a hard print deadline, and tracking hours and margin on a project in progress.

• Type: Contract, with potential to extend based on performance and pipeline.
• Duration: December 2026 through End of April 2027.
• Apx Hours: 20 hrs per week (during 9-6pm business hours)
• Rate: $80 to $100 an hour
• Location: New York preferred, hybrid. Remote considered for exceptional candidates.

Engagement Types

• Annual reports, including print and digital production, printer coordination, and ADA-remediated PDF delivery.

• Proxy statements and related regulated shareholder communications on fixed filing timelines.

• ESG and sustainability reports, including framework-aligned content development and benchmarking.

• Brand identity engagements covering positioning, logo and visual identity systems, brand guidelines, and messaging.

• Website projects, including requirements planning and coordination with development partners.

Core Responsibilities

Client Relationship Management

• Serve as the primary point of contact for senior client stakeholders, including C-suite and investor relations, legal, communications, and marketing leadership.

• Run weekly client check-ins and daily touchpoints during production phases.

• Facilitate brand workshops and working sessions with client leadership.

• Keep conversations at the decision level, protecting the creative team from unnecessary production detail while advocating for the work.

• Maintain organized project records, including meeting recordings, transcripts, and approvals.

Project Management

• Draft scopes of work, project schedules, and production plans, then manage delivery against them.

• Own section-by-section content development cycles, review rounds, and approval workflows.

• Coordinate external vendors including printers, typesetters, proofreaders, accessibility and ADA remediation partners, and media agencies.

• Maintain accurate project status in the agency project management system, including correct project stages and required data fields, so that reporting on hours and financials remains reliable.

• Publish clear daily and weekly status updates that make roles, responsibilities, and next steps unambiguous for the full team.

Financial Management

• Manage project budgets to a 2:1 profitability standard, tracking margin throughout the engagement rather than at close.

• Enter and reconcile contractor and freelance hours accurately.

• Price and write extension SOWs and change orders as scope evolves.

• Keep revenue forecasts and project financial reporting current ahead of weekly internal reviews.

• Flag budget risk early and bring options, not just problems.

Resource Allocation

• Own resource planning and scheduled hours for design, strategy, production, and freelance talent across assigned projects.

• Coordinate shared resources with other engagement leads to avoid overallocation.

• Reassign work and onboard replacement talent without disrupting client timelines or deliverable quality.

Strategic Contribution

• Build project assumptions and plans from provided estimates, adapting them to fit the required commercial range even when the engagement differs from past precedent.

• Sequence work so that upstream approvals are secured before downstream production begins, minimizing rework.

• Identify organic growth opportunities within existing accounts and surface them early.

• Bring formalized process improvements, not just issue identification.

• Seven or more years of project or account management experience in an agency, design studio, or corporate communications environment.

• Demonstrated ownership of annual report or proxy production, including familiarity with fixed filing and print deadlines.

• Experience managing brand identity engagements from discovery through guidelines delivery.

• Proven budget ownership on projects of $250K or greater, with a track record of delivering at or under budget.

• Experience managing freelance and vendor talent, including rate negotiation and hours reconciliation.

• Strong written and verbal communication, with the confidence to push back on clients constructively and make decisions on behalf of the team to maintain momentum.

• Comfort working across strategy, creative, design, production, and finance functions simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications

• Working fluency with AI tools, particularly Claude, for project tracking, deliverable management, meeting preparation, and drafting. AI adoption is a strategic priority for our Creative business unit, and we expect this role to use these tools actively.

• Experience with Kantata or comparable professional services automation platforms.

• Familiarity with sustainability reporting topics and report structures.

• Experience coordinating website builds with external development partners.

• Background in advertising or campaign production, including video and digital media.

• Accessibility and ADA remediation experience for digital documents.

Success Profile

The candidates who succeed in this role are meticulous about detail without becoming bottlenecks. They are friendly but firm with demanding or indecisive clients. They run agenda-driven meetings that end on time with clear next steps. They keep the extended team informed proactively rather than reactively. They treat project financial hygiene as part of the job, not an administrative afterthought. They make the client experience smooth and help the client enjoy the process.

Workplace

Sia values in-person collaboration. When serving clients, consultants may be required to work onsite at a client location based on engagement needs. Between client engagements, consultants are expected to work from a Sia office or approved coworking location at least three days per week. Candidates should reside within a reasonable commuting distance of a Sia office or approved coworking location. Sia maintains offices and coworking arrangements across multiple U.S. markets, including New York City, Charlotte, Greater Seattle, San Francisco Greater Bay Area, Los Angeles, Houston, Atlanta, Baltimore, Chicago, Washington D.C.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of application and throughout their employment. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship now or in the future.

Our Commitment

At Sia, we believe in fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive culture where our employees and partners are valued and thrive in a sense of belonging.

Total Rewards That Support You

Compensation & Pay Transparency

Anticipated Base Salary Range: $94,000 – $140,100 annually.

We're committed to making competitive offers that recognize the unique experience, expertise, and value each candidate brings to our team.

In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for incentive compensation, where applicable, and a comprehensive Total Rewards package that includes health benefits, retirement savings, paid time off, professional development opportunities, and other employee programs.

jobs.title: Cloud Engineer
jobs.description:
Designs, implements, and manages enterprise cloud infrastructure and services, primarily within Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Ensures cloud and supporting Windows infrastructure is reliable, secure, scalable, cost-effective, and aligned with architecture and operational standards. • Designs, deploys, manages, and optimizes GCP infrastructure and core services, including Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, VPC networks, load balancing, Cloud CDN, and related platform components, to meet availability, scalability, performance, and cost requirements.
• Designs and supports Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) environments and collaborates with development teams to integrate, deploy, and operate applications using reliable container and cloud architecture practices.
• Leads or contributes to cloud and infrastructure projects, manages assigned milestones and stakeholder communications, maintains technical and operational documentation, and provides technical guidance and support to IT team members.
• Investigates and resolves complex cloud, server, networking, and platform incidents; evaluates possible causes and recovery options, coordinates escalation when needed, and supports backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity capabilities.
• Designs, administers, and troubleshoots Windows Server and Active Directory services that support cloud and enterprise infrastructure, including integration, authentication, availability, and operational support requirements.
• Monitors cloud infrastructure, logging, capacity, performance, reliability, and cost using GCP tools and Datadog; analyzes trends and exceptions and recommends or implements corrective and optimization actions.
• Automates cloud and infrastructure operations using infrastructure-as-code, GitOps, PowerShell, Python, Bash, Ansible, CI/CD pipelines, Bitbucket, Jenkins, or similar technologies to improve consistency, security, and operational efficiency.

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
• An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential functions of the job.
• Preferred: Google Cloud Professional, Cloud Architect, Professional Data Engineer, or other relevant Google Cloud certification.
• Preferred: Datadog certification or demonstrated hands-on experience with Datadog monitoring and logging.
• Minimum 3 years of relevant cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, or platform engineering experience, including at least 3 years working with Google Cloud Platform.
• Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience with Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) or comparable enterprise Kubernetes platforms.
• Preferred 5 years of progressively responsible cloud and infrastructure engineering experience in an enterprise environment.
• Preferred 5 years experience supporting Windows Server, Active Directory, cloud networking, security, automation, CI/CD, backup, and disaster recovery solutions.
• Strong knowledge of GCP architecture and services, including Compute Engine, Cloud Storage, GKE, VPC, Cloud Load Balancing, Cloud CDN, BigQuery, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, and Cloud Pub/Sub.
• Strong knowledge of Windows Server, Active Directory, cloud networking, identity and access management, encryption, security controls, compliance requirements, backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity practices.
• Ability to analyze ambiguous or complex technical issues, compare alternatives, assess risk and operational impact, and make or recommend sound architecture and troubleshooting decisions.
• Proficiency with infrastructure-as-code, GitOps, PowerShell, Python, Bash, Ansible, CI/CD pipelines, Bitbucket, Datadog, or similar tools.
• Knowledge of DevOps and DevSecOps practices, including integrating security and operational controls into automated delivery pipelines.
• Familiarity with GCP database services, including Cloud SQL, Spanner, Alloy DB, Bigtable, and BigQuery.
• Strong project management, documentation, problem-solving, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills; ability to manage milestones, communicate with stakeholders and management, and provide technical guidance.

jobs.title: American Girl Seasonal Warehouse Associate
jobs.description:
The Opportunity:

The American Girl Distribution Center in DeForest, Wisconsin is seeking Seasonal Warehouse Associates to support operations during our peak business season from October through December. This is a temporary seasonal position designed to provide additional staffing support during the holiday fulfillment period. Employment in this role is intended to last through the seasonal business need and does not guarantee ongoing or regular employment beyond the seasonal assignment period.

Seasonal Warehouse Associates support warehouse fulfillment operations in a fast-paced, automated distribution environment. Associates perform a variety of warehouse functions and are expected to learn and become proficient in all aspects of the fulfillment process while maintaining established safety, quality, and productivity standards.

Successful candidates are dependable, adaptable, and able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. This role requires the ability to perform repetitive tasks, manage multiple responsibilities, and respond to changing business needs and operational priorities.

The regular schedule for this position is 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.; however, work hours are subject to change based on business needs, and occasional weekend shifts may be required during the peak season.

*Note: The last day to interview for this position is 11/18/26

Key Responsibilities:

• Perform a variety of warehouse fulfillment tasks to support daily operations.
• Learn and become proficient in all warehouse functions and work areas.
• Maintain established productivity, quality, and safety standards.
• Accurately complete assigned tasks in a fast-paced warehouse environment.
• Handle multiple tasks simultaneously while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
• Make timely and accurate decisions to support workflow and operational needs.
• Perform repetitive tasks while maintaining consistency and efficiency.
• Adapt to changing priorities and business needs.
• Work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
• Rotate through various warehouse assignments as needed, including unloading trailers and semi-trailers.
• Follow all company policies, procedures, and safety guidelines.

La Oportunidad

El Centro de Distribución de American Girl en DeForest, Wisconsin, está contratando Asociados de Almacén de Temporada para apoyar nuestras operaciones durante la época más ocupada del año, de octubre a diciembre. Esta es una posición temporal creada para brindar apoyo adicional durante la temporada navideña. El empleo está previsto para durar mientras exista la necesidad operativa de temporada y no garantiza empleo permanente una vez finalizada la asignación.

Como Asociado de Almacén de Temporada, formarás parte de un equipo que ayuda a preparar y enviar los pedidos de nuestros clientes en un moderno centro de distribución automatizado. Tendrás la oportunidad de aprender distintas áreas del almacén y desarrollar habilidades en varias etapas del proceso de surtido y envío, siempre siguiendo nuestros estándares de seguridad, calidad y productividad.

Buscamos personas responsables, flexibles y con ganas de aprender, que puedan trabajar bien tanto de manera independiente como en equipo. Este puesto requiere realizar tareas repetitivas, manejar varias responsabilidades al mismo tiempo y adaptarse a las necesidades cambiantes de la operación.

El horario regular de trabajo es de 7:00 a. m. a 3:30 p. m. Sin embargo, los horarios pueden ajustarse de acuerdo con las necesidades del negocio, y podría ser necesario trabajar algunos fines de semana durante la temporada alta.

Nota: El ultimo dia para entrevistar para esta posicion es el 11/18/26

Responsabilidades Principales

• Apoyar las operaciones diarias realizando diferentes tareas dentro del almacén.
• Aprender y desempeñarse en las distintas áreas y funciones del centro de distribución.
• Mantener los estándares de productividad, calidad y seguridad establecidos por la empresa.
• Completar las tareas asignadas con precisión en un ambiente de trabajo dinámico y de ritmo rápido.
• Manejar múltiples tareas al mismo tiempo sin comprometer la calidad del trabajo.
• Tomar decisiones rápidas y acertadas para apoyar el flujo de trabajo y las necesidades operativas.
• Realizar tareas repetitivas de manera constante y eficiente.
• Adaptarse a cambios en las prioridades y necesidades del negocio.
• Trabajar de forma colaborativa con otros miembros del equipo y también de manera independiente cuando sea necesario.
• Rotar entre diferentes áreas de trabajo según las necesidades operativas, incluyendo la descarga de remolques y tráileres.
• Seguir todas las políticas, procedimientos y normas de seguridad de la empresa.

What We're Looking For:

• Must be available to work the full seasonal assignment period, approximately October through December, including schedule changes and occasional weekend shifts as business needs require.
• Ability to frequently lift up to 30 pounds and occasionally lift up to 50 pounds.
• Ability to stand and/or walk on concrete floors for 8 to 10 hours per shift.
• Ability to perform continuous pulling, pushing, grasping, bending, and reaching activities.
• Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and steel-toe shoes.
• Ability and willingness to rotate among all warehouse positions, including unloading trailers and semi-trailers.
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong teamwork and communication skills.
• Ability to adapt to changing operational and scheduling needs.
• Reliable attendance and a commitment to workplace safety.

Lo Que Buscamos

• Disponibilidad para trabajar durante toda la temporada, aproximadamente de octubre a diciembre, incluyendo posibles cambios de horario y algunos turnos de fin de semana según las necesidades del negocio.
• Capacidad para levantar con frecuencia hasta 30 libras y ocasionalmente hasta 50 libras.
• Capacidad para permanecer de pie y/o caminar sobre pisos de concreto durante turnos de 8 a 10 horas.
• Capacidad para realizar de manera continua movimientos de jalar, empujar, agarrar, agacharse y alcanzar objetos.
• Capacidad para usar el equipo de protección personal (PPE) requerido, incluyendo guantes, lentes de seguridad y zapatos con punta de acero.
• Disposición para rotar entre todas las áreas y funciones del almacén, incluyendo la descarga de remolques y tráileres.
• Gran atención a los detalles y compromiso con la precisión en el trabajo.
• Capacidad para desempeñarse de manera efectiva en un entorno de trabajo dinámico y de ritmo acelerado.
• Habilidades sólidas de trabajo en equipo y comunicación.
• Flexibilidad para adaptarse a cambios en las operaciones y los horarios de trabajo.
• Asistencia puntual y confiable, junto con un fuerte compromiso con la seguridad en el lugar de trabajo.

How We Work:

American Girl is subsidiary of Mattel, a purpose driven company aiming to empower generations to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. We live up to our purpose employing the following behaviors:

• We collaborate: Being a part of Mattel means being part of one team with shared values and common goals. Every person counts and working closely together always brings better results. Partnership is our process and our collective capabilities is our superpower.

jobs.title: PMHNP (Adjunct)
jobs.description:
Opportunity at a Glance

Contributing faculty members serve in a part-time capacity to educate Walden University Students by effectively and proficiently using online technology and resources so that knowledge, information, feedback, and critique are imparted to and shared with students in thoughtful, carefully formulated, well written, and timely communications. This is accomplished in an environment that is respectful of student, the Faculty Member, Walden University, and the discipline in which the Faculty Member is involved. Faculty Members are expected to adhere to all Walden University Faculty expectations, which are clearly set forth to the Faculty Member at the start of his/her employment with the University.

Responsibilities

• Training: All new Faculty Members receive specific training from Walden University in the techniques teaching, use of an electronic learning platform, specifics of the policies, procedures and degree programs of the School or College in which they are going to teach, socialization into the Walden University culture, assessment of academic integrity of student work (including use of www.turnitin.com), and research supervision of theses and dissertations.

• Course Teaching: Faculty Members are assigned a course, which is taught using Canvas, and are responsible for interacting with students within this platform. Discussion Boards for classrooms are open 24 hours per day, 7 days per week. Although postings to the classroom may be done at any time of day, they must be completed in a timely manner in accordance with the Faculty Handbook or other criteria established by Walden University. Per the faculty handbook, responses to student questions must be posted within 48 hours. Faculty Members are required to verify the accuracy of student postings and submissions and to provide feedback and grades to students through Canvas. Grading is due within 7 days from the due date of the assignment.

• Availability: Walden expects faculty to be reasonably accessible to students. Faculty members are expected to be available to students outside the course discussion board and in addition to providing substantive feedback on assignments and postings. Faculty members will publish their availability to students through course syllabi, instructor information in the classroom, and/or other appropriate documents. The university suggests regular and predictable availability, such as online office hours or regular online chats.

• Residencies: Faculty Members may be required to attend Residencies held domestically or internationally, (Part-time faculty may, but are not required to attend), where they will teach intensives and colloquia, and facilitate school and university-wide discussions.

• Performs other duties as assigned

• Complies with all policies and standards

• Master's Degree in the field of study or closely related field (or recognized by a country’s Ministry of Education or Counsel of Higher Education). Required

• Active, unencumbered PMHNP certification.

• Minnesota RN and APRN licenses, or willingness to obtain these licenses as a condition of employment.

• 1 year of clinical practice as a PMHNP. Required.

• Faculty members are required to have an adequate computer to handle an electronic learning platform, keyboard, pointing device, and computer monitor. All other tools are knowledge-based or training-based through Walden University. The Faculty Member must be able to use Microsoft Office products (MS Word, MS Excel, and MS PowerPoint), zip software, and Adobe Acrobat and must have reliable Internet access as well as alternate access in cases where primary access becomes unavailable.

• Candidates should possess a significant record of intellectual and professional contributions to the field of College of Nursing, including experience in the practice of Psychology Mental Health.

• Commitment to advocating for the learning and development needs of students earning their degrees in a distance learning environment.

• Teaching, advising and mentoring; commitment to the promotion of applied research and the recruitment and development of a diverse faculty; excellent leadership, communication, team, and human relations skills.

• Experience with distance learning preferred.

• Faculty Members must be appropriately credentialed, possess an earned degree from an accredited institution or recognized by a country's ministry of education in the discipline being taught, and may be expected to be licensed or license-eligible in order to teach in specific programs.

• Faculty Members must maintain their licenses and any appropriate certifications in order to continue to teach at Walden University.

• Faculty Members are also expected to maintain currency with research by reviewing articles, journals, and presentations. If participating in research, the Faculty Member may publish and acknowledge Walden University.

In support of the pay transparency laws enacted across the country, the expected compensation rate for this position is as follows:

• Graduate Course Instruction: $1,560 - $4,080 per Quarter or Semester, depending on type of course taught and length of course
• Undergraduate Course Instruction: $700 - $2,200 per quarter, depending on type of course taught and length of course Actual pay may be adjusted based on job-related factors permitted by law, such as type of course taught; experience and training; geographic location; licensure and certifications; market factors; departmental budgets; and responsibility. Walden also offers other opportunities for its adjunct faculty members, such as dissertation/doctoral study committee chair positions, research reviewing, and dissertation and doctoral study mentoring.

Equal Opportunity – Minority / Female / Disability / V / Gender Identity / Sexual Orientation

jobs.title: Senior Director Package & Assembly Engineering
jobs.description:
The Sr. Director, will lead organization responsible for driving execution of packaging development, new product introduction and assembly engineering continuous improvement. This leader will partner closely with Package Design and Development Engineering Directors, product group partners—especially Design, Application, and Marketing teams—Product, Reliability, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, and key OSAT/CM partners to ensure programs meet committed schedules, quality and reliability objectives, production readiness requirements and long term continuous improvement of packaging products. The role will establish strong program governance, identify and escalate critical risks early, and lead cross-functional technical task forces to resolve development challenges that threaten quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, or schedule. Additionally, the role will closely monitor operations at our key OSAT partners, ensuring consistent execution, effective issue escalation, and tight alignment between Renesas development teams and external assembly partners.

Responsibilities:

• Recruit, build and mentor a new team of Packaging engineers.
• Partner with Package Engineering Directors who lead technical package development programs, providing program-level execution leadership, governance, and accountability.
• Establish and drive end-to-end NPI program plans, milestones, critical paths, resource alignment, risk management, and executive reporting to ensure committed schedules are achieved.
• Create a disciplined program management operating model covering development, qualification, customer requirements, production readiness, ramp, and transition to volume manufacturing.
• Proactively identify technical, quality, reliability, supply, manufacturing, and schedule risks; establish mitigation plans and escalate critical issues with clear recommendations and decision points.
• Lead cross-functional technical task forces for major development challenges, particularly issues affecting quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, qualification, or NPI schedule.
• Drive structured problem solving and closure of critical issues using data-driven methods, root-cause analysis, risk assessment, and clearly defined corrective/preventive actions.
• Coordinate closely with Package Engineering, product group partners—especially Design, Application, and Marketing teams—Product Engineering, Reliability, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain, and other functional leaders to remove execution barriers and maintain program momentum.
• Establish program dashboards and management systems that provide transparent visibility to milestones, critical path activities, risks, issues, action owners, and recovery plans.
• Lead technical program management activities with key OSAT/CM partners, including program reviews, milestone tracking, issue escalation, recovery plans, qualification readiness, and production ramp execution.
• Ensure execution of Engineering Build Requests (EBRs) per committed schedule at each OSAT, regularly tracking overall EBR progress, identifying delays, and driving timely recovery actions.
• Develop and lead package and assembly teams located at strategic OSATs, ensuring alignment with Renesas priorities, technical teams, and global NPI schedules.
• Ensure OSAT/CM development activities, DOE, process optimization, qualification, process-window verification, production controls, and ramp readiness are aligned with overall NPI program objectives.
• Drive timely resolution of process integration and assembly issues that could impact product quality, reliability, qualification, yield, or customer commitments.
• Ensure effective transition from development and qualification into production, including readiness reviews, ramp monitoring, issue management, and sustained execution.
• Establish standardized program management processes, templates, metrics, escalation mechanisms, and lessons-learned practices across the global organization.
• Provide concise, fact-based executive communication on program health, critical risks, schedule recovery, resource needs, and decisions required from senior leadership.
• Build strong relationships with OSAT/CM executive and technical leadership to improve responsiveness, accountability, and execution of critical AI/Datacenter Power programs.
• Develop the technical and leadership capabilities of the TPM organization and establish a high-performance, execution-focused culture.
• Support package technology roadmap execution by translating strategic technology priorities into executable development programs, milestones, resources, and deliverables.
• Address internal and external customer-impacting issues in partnership with Marketing, Product, Quality, Operations, and Package Engineering organizations.

LEADERSHIP & ORGANIZATIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES

• Recruit, build and mentor a new team of Packaging engineers.
• Lead and develop a team of Package and assembly engineers supporting multiple package types and business groups
• Set organizational priorities, staffing strategy, performance expectations, and development plans aligned with business growth.
• Establish clear accountability between Package Development Engineering, NPI Engineering, OSAT engineering technical leaders while avoiding duplication of technical ownership.
• Create a culture of urgency, fact-based decision making, cross-functional collaboration, ownership, and rapid issue resolution.
• Drive consistent execution standards across internal teams and strategic OSAT locations.

• Location Commitment: Willingness and ability to relocate to / be based in India for a 2-year project assignment.
• Doctorate, Master’s, or Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, or a related technical discipline.
• 15–20+ years of relevant experience in semiconductor engineering, product development, applications, package development, NPI, manufacturing, technical program management, or a closely related field.
• Demonstrated experience leading complex semiconductor NPI programs involving package development, assembly, qualification, reliability, and manufacturing ramp.
• Strong understanding of semiconductor product development process, package and assembly processes.
• Experience working with OSATs/CMs and managing complex development and production activities across geographically distributed organizations.
• Proven track record leading cross-functional technical task forces and resolving complex issues involving quality, reliability, yield, manufacturability, and schedule.
• Strong understanding of qualification, reliability, SPC/statistical methods, process development, risk management, and structured problem-solving methodologies.
• Exceptional program management skills, including critical-path management, risk management, executive escalation, schedule recovery, and cross-functional resource alignment.
• Strong interpersonal, communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
• Ability to influence senior technical and business leaders without direct authority and drive accountability across organizational boundaries.
• Experience building and leading global teams, including teams in product groups, embedded at external manufacturing or OSAT locations.
• Strong analytical skills and ability to translate complex technical issues into clear business impact, decisions, and actions.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience supporting high-growth customer programs.
• Experience with formal technical program management methodologies and portfolio-level governance.
• Experience driving customer-critical NPI programs in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

SUCCESS MEASURES

• On-time achievement of NPI milestones and customer commitments.
• Reduction in schedule delays caused by unresolved technical, quality, reliability, or manufacturing issues.
• Timely closure of critical cross-functional task-force actions.
• Improved qualification, yield, reliability, and production-readiness performance.
• Effective execution and alignment of strategic OSAT/CM partners.
• Development of a high-performing Packaging Development and Assebly Engineering organization and standardized program-management operating model.

jobs.description:
At this time, Palos Hospital is not considering external ADN candidates for our RN openings. We appreciate your interest in Northwestern Medicine and encourage you to apply to other opportunities at https://jobs.nm.org/. Internal employee ADN candidates are still encouraged to apply.

The Staff Nurse reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• The registered professional nurse assumes accountability and responsibility for the individualized, age-specific care of a patient along the continuum from admission to discharge. She/He gives direct care to assigned patients and assists with other patient care when necessary. The registered professional nurse’s decisions and actions on behalf of the patient/family are determined in an ethical manner. She/He collects and analyzes the assessment data in determining nursing diagnoses, collaborates with the patient/family and other health care team members, develops a plan of care to attain realistic outcomes, provides education founded on evidence-based practice, and systematically evaluates the quality and effectiveness of nursing practice.

Responsibilities:

• Assess and records patient status and identifies patient care needs upon admission/point of care entry.
• Organizes the assessment health data so that it is accurate, complete and accessible.
• Identifies problems that need immediate attention.
• Validates diagnoses with patient/family and other health care team members.
• Documents diagnoses in a manner that facilitates the determination of expected outcomes and plan of care.
• Initiates Problem List at the time of admission and updates as needed. Incorporates principles of age-specific care into the patient’s plan of care.
• Documents that the patient’s individualized plan of care has been discussed with and agreed upon by the patient/family.
• Begins plans for discharge at time of admission; consults with patient/family and health care team members regarding discharge plan.
• Identifies patient teaching needs on admission and throughout hospital stay.
• Arranges conferences with patient and/or family and other members of health team when indicated to plan care.
• Prioritizes and organizes nursing interventions that are evidence based and reflective of established standards of care.
• Provides individualized, mutually agreeable, patient and family education that is founded on evidence-based practice and research guidelines.
• Documents all assessments, interventions and patient responses.
• Reviews consistently the patient’s health data to keep the Plan of Care updated.
• Assures that revisions to the plan of care are systematic and ongoing and are driven by measurable realistic goals.
• Documents the patient’s progression toward identified outcomes
• Identifies unmet outcomes and provides direction for continuity of care.
• Reassesses nursing actions for effectiveness in achieving desired outcomes.
• Communicates with patient/family and health care team members re: patient care and nursing’s role in the provision of care.
• Collaborates with patient/family and healthcare team members re: the patient’s progress/plan of care.
• Presents relevant patient information at multidisciplinary meetings/conferences for feedback from peers.
• Makes appropriate referrals as needed for continuity of care.

Required:

• Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN)
• Current State of Illinois Registered Professional Nurse
• American Heart Association Basic Life Support (BLS)
• Strong interpersonal skills
• Ability to collaborate with others
• Strong analytic abilities
• Associate Degree Nursing (ADN) acceptable with commitment to obtain a BSN from an accredited program within three years of first day of employment in clinical nurse role.
