jobs.title: CX Ops Specialist
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a CX Operations Specialist, you’re the first point of contact for customers’ billing and account needs, and you build the automation that makes the whole Customer Experience team faster. You’ll resolve billing disputes, handle account and SSO setup, and own monthly credit and renewal reporting. You’ll work closely with Commerce, Billing, and Finance as well as directly with customers. In this role, empathy and clear communication matter as much as the technical work.

This is a role where you’ll spend roughly half your time on support and reporting and the other half building. You’ll find the repeatable, rules-based steps in the work, starting with refund request triage, and turn them into agent skills and workflows that produce accurate, reliable results. You’ll also partner with Commerce and engineering to turn friction in support-side billing workflows into clear requirements.

You will be the first hire in a new function on a growing team. As the day-to-day gets automated, there’s room to grow into ownership of areas like RCA deliverables, CSAT, and renewals, or to go deeper as a technical tools and automation specialist.

This role is based out of our SF headquarters and hybrid.

Responsibilities

• Own billing and account support: triage, respond, and resolve, or route to the right team

• Process refunds, investigate disputed charges, and resolve payment declines, payment-method changes, negative balances, and credit-limit issues

• Handle account setup, including SSO configuration for common identity providers (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace), and diagnose common failures

• Manage monthly reporting of customer credit requests, supporting forecasting and detailed customer reports checked against contract terms

• Build and maintain agent skills that automate repeatable steps of billing and credit work, starting with refund request triage

• Work with the Commerce team on product delivery, credit deposits, order fulfillment, and endpoint reservations, using internal systems and command-line tools

• Raise friction in support-side billing workflows and help turn it into clear requirements

• Agree on priorities with your manager based on hours saved and error reduction

Requirements

• Experience in a customer-facing support, customer success, billing support, program management, or operations role, or equivalent projects. We care more about what you’ve built and the problems you’ve solved than the number of years.

• A knack for breaking problems into core pieces and turning recurring patterns into clear rules and steps that an automated workflow can follow

• Comfort working in a terminal: running commands, reading curl or HTTP requests, and interpreting JSON error responses

• Strong written communication and genuine empathy, with the ability to explain billing and technical concepts to non-technical customers

• Attention to detail with numbers: you check totals, reconcile sources, and catch discrepancies

• Experience owning a ticket queue in a support platform (Pylon, Zendesk, Intercom, or similar) and working to response and resolution targets

• A strong sense of ownership and a habit of documenting what you learn and fixing root causes instead of repeating the same fix

• Ability to manage multiple workstreams and switch context frequently

Preferred Qualifications

• Golang or Rust development experience

• Experience building and managing cloud-native services (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud Platform)

• Strong understanding of Linux system and networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, kernel operations, memory, and file system management

• Familiarity with Open Compute Project (OCP) technologies (OpenBMC, Coreboot, Linuxboot, etc.)

If you don’t meet every requirement but believe you’d be a great fit, we’d still love to hear from you. We’re looking for part support, part PM, part engineer.

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

Compensation

We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance and other competitive benefits. The US base salary range for this full-time position is: $140K - $180K + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.

Application Policy

Please read each role carefully and apply to the position best suited to you. Candidates are limited to 6 applications within a 90-day period, and applications beyond that limit will be automatically rejected. You may apply to additional roles 90 days after your last application.

Equal Opportunity

Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more.

Please see our privacy policy at https://www.together.ai/privacy.

jobs.title: Principal Propulsion Engineer- Components
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

Varda is hiring an experienced Principal Propulsion Engineer- Components to join the team that designs, builds, tests, and flies the fluid components on the W-Series satellite bus and future vehicles. The W-Series satellite incorporates a high-test hydrogen peroxide (HTP) and hydrocarbon bipropellant propulsion system with high-pressure inert gas pressurization and cold-gas attitude control. The component portfolio spans each of these fluid subsystems and includes solenoid control valves, check valves, relief valves, burst disks, fluid filters, regulators, manually operated service valves, machined fluid manifolds, and instrumentation including pressure transducers and RTDs.  A successful candidate will take on a significant share of the component ownership for these mission-critical hardware articles as responsible engineer, helping expand component capabilities, improve reliability, and increase flight cadence.

Many current Varda components are purchased parts, and you will be a primary technical interface to our suppliers. Varda also intends to bring more component design in-house for current and future vehicles, and you will help lead that transition: shaping make-versus-buy decisions, executing detailed design, and standing up the capabilities to develop, qualify, produce, acceptance test, and fly Varda-owned parts. As part of a broad, multi-disciplinary engineering team, you will interface daily with propulsion systems, structures, production, thermal, avionics, and GNC engineers and technicians.  You will inherit an operational, well-documented component baseline and drive improvements alongside the team. The role is hands-on: test stand development and operations, production floor support, occasional supplier visits, and issue or anomaly investigations as required.  Bring your experience and passion, and let’s build something amazing.

Responsibilities

• Serve as responsible engineer for a significant portion of the bus propulsion component portfolio, from requirements and specification generation through development, qualification, production, and flight, in partnership with the broader engineering team

• Design Varda-owned propulsion components: CAD, detailed drawings with GD&T per ASME Y14.5, tolerance analysis, seal and spring design, and supporting structural and fluid analysis

• Specify, source, and qualify purchased components; serve as a technical lead with suppliers, review qualification and acceptance data, and drive corrective action and/or second sourcing

• Author and execute acceptance and qualification test (ATP/QTP) campaigns per SMC-S-016; characterize component performance across the pressure and temperature envelope and feed results back into system requirements; document results with clear test reports

• Support vehicle build, integration and test, and flight operations: disposition nonconformances and lead component issue or anomaly investigations to root cause and closure

• Represent your components in design reviews, FMEAs, hazard analyses, and range safety interactions; contribute to the shared component knowledge base, qualification records, and lessons learned

• Mentor engineers and help set the component design and test standards the propulsion team relies and builds on

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent professional experience considered

• 6+ years of hands-on experience designing, qualifying, or owning fluid components (valves, regulators, filters, burst disks, manifolds, transducers) for spacecraft, launch vehicles, or comparable high-pressure hardware, on either the vehicle or the component-supplier side

• Working understanding of component design fundamentals: sealing, force balance, spring sizing, friction, flow paths, materials compatibility, material finishes, and wear

• Mechanical design proficiency: CAD, assembly management using PLM software, detailed drawings with GD&T per ASME Y14.5, and tolerance analysis

• Experience with component pressure and leak testing and ATP/QTP execution per SMC-S-016 or an equivalent standard, including authoring procedures and establishing pass/fail criteria

• Hands-on experience building and testing pressurized hardware alongside technicians

• Proven record of technical ownership: driving nonconformances and anomalies to root cause and corrective action across teams and suppliers

• Willingness to travel to suppliers and test sites as needed (typically < 10% of time)

Preferred Skills and Experience

• 10+ years of spacecraft or launch vehicle fluid component experience, including clean-sheet design of a valve, regulator, or similar component through qualification and flight

• Experience with low-leakage, on-orbit propulsion components and with HTP, other strong oxidizers, or high-pressure gas systems

• Analysis skills for component design: FEA of pressure-containing parts, 1D fluid network modeling, valve dynamics, and fatigue and fracture control

• Electromechanical and instrumentation fundamentals: solenoid valve coil and driver interfaces, and pressure transducer and RTD calibration, excitation, and error budgets

• Supplier management for COTS and build-to-print aerospace components: source selection, audits, and data package review

• Familiarity with AIAA S-080 and S-081 and AFSPCMAN 91-710 range safety requirements

• Knowledge of precision manufacturing and inspection for fluid hardware: machining and deburring, welding, electropolish, precision cleaning, CMM, and NDE

• Experience standing up testing capabilities for propulsion components (dev, qual, ATP), particularly in a high-cadence, high component throughput environment.

• Prior experience leading a technical sub-discipline, formally or informally, and developing engineering standards within a propulsion organization

• Exceptional technical communication skills, precision and clarity in specifications, test procedures, data package reviews, and engineering memos

Pay Range

• Salary Range: Principal: $181,913 – $232,444/per year

jobs.title: Senior Propulsion Engineer- Components
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

Varda is hiring an experienced Senior Propulsion Engineer- Components to join the team that designs, builds, tests, and flies the fluid components on the W-Series satellite bus and future vehicles. The W-Series satellite incorporates a high-test hydrogen peroxide (HTP) and hydrocarbon bipropellant propulsion system with high-pressure inert gas pressurization and cold-gas attitude control. The component portfolio spans each of these fluid subsystems and includes solenoid control valves, check valves, relief valves, burst disks, fluid filters, regulators, manually operated service valves, machined fluid manifolds, and instrumentation including pressure transducers and RTDs.  A successful candidate will take on a significant share of the component ownership for these mission-critical hardware articles as responsible engineer, helping expand component capabilities, improve reliability, and increase flight cadence.

Many current Varda components are purchased parts, and you will be a primary technical interface to our suppliers. Varda also intends to bring more component design in-house for current and future vehicles, and you will help lead that transition: shaping make-versus-buy decisions, executing detailed design, and standing up the capabilities to develop, qualify, produce, acceptance test, and fly Varda-owned parts. As part of a broad, multi-disciplinary engineering team, you will interface daily with propulsion systems, structures, production, thermal, avionics, and GNC engineers and technicians.  You will inherit an operational, well-documented component baseline and drive improvements alongside the team. The role is hands-on: test stand development and operations, production floor support, occasional supplier visits, and issue or anomaly investigations as required.  Bring your experience and passion, and let’s build something amazing.

Responsibilities

• Serve as responsible engineer for a significant portion of the bus propulsion component portfolio, from requirements and specification generation through development, qualification, production, and flight, in partnership with the broader engineering team

• Design Varda-owned propulsion components: CAD, detailed drawings with GD&T per ASME Y14.5, tolerance analysis, seal and spring design, and supporting structural and fluid analysis

• Specify, source, and qualify purchased components; serve as a technical lead with suppliers, review qualification and acceptance data, and drive corrective action and/or second sourcing

• Author and execute acceptance and qualification test (ATP/QTP) campaigns per SMC-S-016; characterize component performance across the pressure and temperature envelope and feed results back into system requirements; document results with clear test reports

• Support vehicle build, integration and test, and flight operations: disposition nonconformances and lead component issue or anomaly investigations to root cause and closure

• Represent your components in design reviews, FMEAs, hazard analyses, and range safety interactions; contribute to the shared component knowledge base, qualification records, and lessons learned

• Mentor engineers and help set the component design and test standards the propulsion team relies and builds on

Basic Qualifications

• B.S. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline; equivalent professional experience considered

• 3+ years of hands-on experience designing, qualifying, or owning fluid components (valves, regulators, filters, burst disks, manifolds, transducers) for spacecraft, launch vehicles, or comparable high-pressure hardware, on either the vehicle or the component-supplier side

• Working understanding of component design fundamentals: sealing, force balance, spring sizing, friction, flow paths, materials compatibility, material finishes, and wear

• Mechanical design proficiency: CAD, assembly management using PLM software, detailed drawings with GD&T per ASME Y14.5, and tolerance analysis

• Experience with component pressure and leak testing and ATP/QTP execution per SMC-S-016 or an equivalent standard, including authoring procedures and establishing pass/fail criteria

• Hands-on experience building and testing pressurized hardware alongside technicians

• Proven record of technical ownership: driving nonconformances and anomalies to root cause and corrective action across teams and suppliers

• Willingness to travel to suppliers and test sites as needed (typically < 10% of time)

Preferred Skills and Experience

• 6+ years of spacecraft or launch vehicle fluid component experience, including clean-sheet design of a valve, regulator, or similar component through qualification and flight

• Experience with low-leakage, on-orbit propulsion components and with HTP, other strong oxidizers, or high-pressure gas systems

• Analysis skills for component design: FEA of pressure-containing parts, 1D fluid network modeling, valve dynamics, and fatigue and fracture control

• Electromechanical and instrumentation fundamentals: solenoid valve coil and driver interfaces, and pressure transducer and RTD calibration, excitation, and error budgets

• Supplier management for COTS and build-to-print aerospace components: source selection, audits, and data package review

• Familiarity with AIAA S-080 and S-081 and AFSPCMAN 91-710 range safety requirements

• Knowledge of precision manufacturing and inspection for fluid hardware: machining and deburring, welding, electropolish, precision cleaning, CMM, and NDE

• Experience standing up testing capabilities for propulsion components (dev, qual, ATP), particularly in a high-cadence, high component throughput environment.

• Prior experience leading a technical sub-discipline, formally or informally, and developing engineering standards within a propulsion organization

• Exceptional technical communication skills, precision and clarity in specifications, test procedures, data package reviews, and engineering memos

Pay Range

Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

jobs.title: Government Cloud Security Engineer
jobs.location: Austin, TX; New York, NY; Palo Alto, CA; Washington, DC
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

GOVERNMENT CLOUD SECURITY ENGINEER

We are seeking a skilled Government Cloud Security Engineer to design, implement, and maintain robust security controls across our Federal environments (including hybrid and multi-cloud scenarios). In this hands-on role, you will build, strengthen, and maintain our security posture, protect critical workloads, and collaborate with engineering, DevOps, and compliance teams to embed security throughout the development lifecycle. You will develop, implement, and leverage a range of security tools to detect threats, respond to incidents, and ensure alignment with industry standards and regulations. Lastly, you will be required to both achieve and maintain compliance with government regulations such as FedRAMP and CMMC.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Design, implement, and manage security architecture for federal and DoD deployments across cloud and on-premises environments, aligned to FedRAMP High, DoD IL5/IL6, and NIST SP 800-53 controls

• Implement and operate security tooling and services such as SIEM and log pipelines, EDR, vulnerability scanners, container runtime security, and policy-as-code enforcement

• Building secure containerized, Kubernetes-managed environments leveraging Zero Trust principles

• Secure Linux hosts, Kubernetes clusters, virtualization, and databases, including PKI and TLS, SSH and bastion access, and OS-level auditing

• Design and enforce identity and access management, including SSO and federation, phishing-resistant MFA, RBAC, just-in-time privileged access, and periodic access reviews

• Partner with network teams to secure firewalls, VPN and IPsec, DNS, load balancers and reverse proxies, VLAN and subnet segmentation, and routing and switching ACLs

• Protect data encryption at rest and in transit, including envelope encryption and key management

• Harden operating systems, network devices, databases, and container platforms against DISA STIGs and CIS Benchmarks, and run credentialed vulnerability and compliance scanning to keep them compliant over time

• Perform detection, threat hunting, incident response, and root cause analysis, working with the SOC, maintain and exercise the incident response plan, and meet federal incident reporting requirements (e.g., CISA, DoD)

• Own continuous monitoring end to end, including monthly vulnerability scanning and reporting, deviation requests, and driving POA&M items through remediation and closure

• Support ATO packages and assessments, including System Security Plan (SSP) and control implementation documentation, 3PAO and DISA assessor evidence requests, and significant change requests

• Partner with developers and architects to build DevSecOps practices, including secure CI/CD pipelines, secure defaults, and security review of Infrastructure as Code, container images, and Kubernetes deployments before they ship

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Active U.S. security clearance (e.g., Secret, Top Secret) or eligibility to obtain one

• 3+ years of hands-on experience in cloud security, cybersecurity, DevSecOps, or infrastructure engineering with a security focus

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Microsoft Certified: Azure Security Engineer Associate (AZ-500) or Cybersecurity Architect (SC-100), or other relevant certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, AWS Security Specialty, or GIAC (e.g., GCLD, GCIH)

• Hands-on experience with Azure security services (Defender, Sentinel, Entra ID, Azure Policy, Key Vault, Purview) and with on-prem Linux, Kubernetes, and network infrastructure (Palo Alto, Cisco, Juniper)

• Experience with detection and response engineering and SOC operations

• Knowledge of container and Kubernetes security, software supply chain security (image signing, hardened base images), or AI/ML workload protection

• Experience supporting FedRAMP High or DoD IL5/IL6 authorizations, including continuous monitoring and assessor interactions

• Hands-on expertise in building and maintaining secure infrastructure from the ground up in both cloud or on-prem environments

• Proficiency in scripting/automation (PowerShell, Azure CLI, Bicep/ARM templates, Terraform)

• Strong understanding of identity federation, zero-trust principles, encryption, network security, and vulnerability management

• Familiarity with compliance frameworks (NIST, CMMC, STIGs, etc.) and regulatory requirements

• Excellent problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills

• Strong verbal and written communication skills and the ability to stay composed under pressure

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$100,000 - $198,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI, which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

Learn more about the ITAR here.

jobs.title: Master Scheduler
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril's Planning team is seeking a world-class Master Scheduler to join our team. The Master Scheduler has an integral role at Anduril, serving as the link between program leadership and the Production, Engineering, and Supply Chain teams that build our hardware. They will have full ownership of the top-level master schedule, translating program objectives into achievable build targets, and will be ultimately responsible for making sure the factory is working to the right plan at the right time. This hire will be instrumental in setting planning targets within our ERP/MRP systems, tracking actuals and forecasts against the schedule, and surfacing BOM configuration issues and production risks early enough to act on them.

The right person for this role has demonstrated ownership and experience scheduling complex hardware programs in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. They can interpret signals from across the company, understand critical path drivers, and turn them into clear recommendations for leadership. If you are someone who thrives under pressure and enjoys bringing order to complexity, then this role is for you!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own top-level production signals for designated product lines, and expand the master schedule to new products as they come online.

• Build a deep understanding of the production system, processes, and capacity, and ensure production needs are accurately reflected in the master schedule.

• Identify upcoming schedule, BOM configuration, and production constraints, and collaborate with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing to develop tactical actions that keep the factory on schedule.

• Run scenario and risk models for hardware allocation, weighing new builds against refurbished or reworked units to keep pace with changing customer delivery schedules and program demands.

• Partner with Production teams on the shop floor to implement best practices in supply and material flow.

• Work with Supply Chain, Production, and Engineering to understand their requirements and build them into target plans.

• Drive efficient, accurate, and timely propagation of schedule changes across the organization.

• Resolve top-level BOM configuration, critical path, and lead-time discrepancies, from root cause through solution implementation.

• Lead process stabilization and improvement initiatives across planning and scheduling.

• Develop and report on metrics that demonstrate schedule accountability, process stability, and continuous improvement.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in a technical field (e.g. manufacturing, engineering, analytics, computer science) or business field (e.g. supply chain management, operations, business administration).

• 5+ years of professional experience, including 3+ years as a scheduler or scheduling manager in a technical organization.

• 2+ years of experience generating development and production schedules.

• Experience in a fast-paced manufacturing or logistics environment with complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies.

• Ability to travel up to 10% of the time.

• Ability to relocate, if not already local, to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience supporting design engineering and R&D teams through the transition from development to production.

• Experience with ERP/MRP systems such as Oracle or NetSuite.

• Experience with SQL or other custom queries for schedule and production metrics.

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

• Ability to take in large quantities of information and present it clearly and concisely to leadership.

• Ability to work with limited supervision to develop and manage program plans and schedules.

• Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to be diplomatically persuasive or assertive when necessary.

• Proactive self-starter who learns quickly and takes initiative, with a focus on speed and accuracy.

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret/TS security clearance.

US Salary Range

$117,000—$154,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Senior Response Engineer - Cloudflare Managed Defense Center (CMDC)
jobs.description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Location: Singapore

About the Department

Cloudforce One is Cloudflare's threat operations and research team, responsible for identifying and disrupting cyber threats ranging from sophisticated cyber criminal activity to nation-state sponsored advanced persistent threats (APTs). Cloudforce One works in close partnership with external organizations and internal Cloudflare teams, continuously developing operational tradecraft and expanding ever-growing sources of threat intelligence to enable expedited threat hunting and remediation.

Members of Cloudforce One are at the helm of leveraging an incredibly vast and varied set of data points that only one of the world's largest global networks can provide. The team analyzes these unique data points at massive scale and efficiency, synthesizing findings into actionable threat intelligence to better protect our customers.

About INTERDICT

I.N.T.E.R.D.I.C.T. (Identify, Neutralize, Triage, Engage, Respond, Disrupt, Integrate, Contain, Threat Hunting) is Cloudforce One's unified operational security organization responsible for identifying, analyzing, and responding to threats targeting Cloudflare and its customers. INTERDICT encompasses three main sub-functions:

• Cloudflare Managed Defense (CMD): Network and application security monitoring for 'Under Attack' mitigation support.

• PhishGuard: Managed email threat detection and response service.

• Detection Engineering: ML model development and detection optimization.

Together, INTERDICT provides comprehensive 24×7×365 protection across email, application, and network threat surfaces.

Role Summary

As a Senior Response Engineer within the Cloudflare Managed Defense Center (CMDC), you will serve as a subject-matter expert and technical escalation point for threat mitigation across Cloudflare’s strategic enterprise customer base. In this role, you will lead the response to sophisticated, multi-vector cyberattacks spanning OSI Layers 3, 4, and 7, operating beyond standard playbooks to diagnose anomalies, engineer custom mitigations, and stabilize mission-critical infrastructure under fire.

Beyond active incident command, you will act as a force multiplier: architecting customer-specific defense strategies, authoring and refining automated detection logic, mentoring Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers, and collaborating directly with Cloudflare Product and Engineering teams. We are looking for an experienced, high-ownership technical leader who excels during high-stakes incidents and is passionate about mentoring others while advancing threat mitigation at scale.

CMDC operates 24×7×365. This role participates in a regional shift rotation and on-call escalation rota including periodic weekend and public-holiday coverage as part of a follow-the-sun model across AMER, EMEA, and APAC.

Role Responsibilities

• Act as the technical lead and incident commander during high-impact, multi-vector security events, designing and deploying bespoke mitigation strategies when standard runbooks do not suffice.

• Perform deep-dive forensic analysis into complex Layer 3/4 and Layer 7 traffic anomalies, identifying zero-day attack patterns, sophisticated bot networks, and novel evasion techniques.

• Apply advanced mitigation strategies and filter malicious traffic using Cloudflare’s core security suite, including Magic Transit, Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Advanced Rate Limiting.

• Lead technical communications and incident bridge calls with enterprise C-level executives, principal network engineers, and security teams during critical events, clearly articulating root causes, impact assessments, and remediation paths.

• Monitor and investigate proactive security alerts across internal telemetry systems to rapidly triage incoming events, assess blast radius, and validate threat severity.

• Adhere to and champion strict customer SLAs for alert response times, event analysis, and clear executive reporting.

• Mentor and elevate Tier 1 and Tier 2 engineers through structured shadowing, technical post-mortems, and internal training.

• Partner with internal Engineering and Product teams to translate operational attack trends into prioritized platform enhancements, tool feedback, and automated detection logic.

Role Requirements (Must-Have Skills)

• A minimum of 6–8 years of hands-on experience in a high-volume Security Operations Center (SOC), Managed Detection and Response (MDR), network engineering, or incident response environment dealing directly with live threat mitigation.

• Comprehensive knowledge of networking principles and internet infrastructure, including TCP/IP, UDP, ICMP, DNS, BGP routing mechanics, and edge network design.

• Deep expertise in Layer 7 protocols and web architectures (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, TLS handshakes/ciphers, reverse proxy models, and API security).

• Experience analyzing network traffic data for anomaly detection and designing, tuning, and executing advanced mitigation strategies against L3/L4 and L7 attacks, including bespoke countermeasures when standard playbooks are insufficient.

• Advanced proficiency in packet capture and network traffic analysis using tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, or tshark to isolate anomalies and dissect malformed or novel payloads.

• Practical experience analyzing and mitigating security incidents using AI and machine learning tools, paired with the hands-on capability to build and integrate custom tooling that improves operational workflows, accelerates log telemetry analysis, and defends against AI-driven botnets and adversarial edge attacks.

• Proficiency in using the command line (Bash shell) alongside general system administration literacy across Linux, Mac, or Windows environments.

• Proven experience commanding incident bridges, making decisive risk-tradeoff decisions, and maintaining composure while managing enterprise stakeholders during high-pressure crises.

Nice-to-Have Skills

• Direct experience querying large-scale distributed logging and analytics systems using SQL, GraphQL, ClickHouse, or SIEM platforms (Splunk, Elastic, Sumo Logic).

• Hands-on experience defending against advanced persistent threats (APTs), credential stuffing, scraping botnets, or application-layer bypass attacks against major CDNs/WAFs.

• Relevant industry certifications, such as CISSP, CCNP/CCIE, or advanced GIAC credentials (e.g., GCIA, GCIH, GNFA).

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Emergency Veterinarian (Part Time) - Larkspur, CA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a part-time Emergency Veterinarian, you’re more than just passionate about helping people and their pets; you thrive on it, especially when they need you most. At VEG, we find a way to say yes to supporting you, so you can be the best, most confident ER professional possible and grow your career in unexpected directions. With a culture rooted in mentorship and continuous learning—from on-the-floor guidance to VEG Education programs and unlimited ER-focused CE—you’ll never stop learning. You’ll handle any emergency that comes through the door, from routine cases to complex surgeries, and treat every kind of pet, including exotics! As a leader on the hospital floor, you’ll have the chance to be a superhero for your customers, backed by a team and resources that empower you to take your career further than you ever imagined.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Answer medical questions over the phone

• See patients right away as part of the VEG Triage and VEG Spikes, our unique, customer-centered way of doing things—like ensuring people see a doctor right away and allowing families to stay with their pets

• Gather the signalment, presenting complaint, vitals, and physical exam

• Conduct physical examinations of animals, along with other required investigatory measures such as ultrasounds, X-rays, bloodwork, and biopsies

• Complete a diagnosis of each pet's condition to create a diagnostic and therapeutic plan

• Communicate diagnosis and treatment options directly with customers

• Prepare estimates and present them to customers

• Create and review medical records to ensure accuracy

• Demonstrate the value of tests and treatments performed by speaking with the customer and addressing their concerns

• Perform minor and major emergency surgeries

• Perform endoscopic procedures

• Educate customers on after care and preventative measures where appropriate

WHAT YOU NEED

• A DVM or equivalent degree

• Live and breathe emergency medicine, including emergency surgery (the soft tissue kind!) and endoscopy

• Thrive in team-oriented environments (think hospital retreats, team dinners, happy hours, and more)

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

About Ceribell

Ceribell is a medical technology company focused on transforming the diagnosis and management of patients with serious neurological conditions. The Ceribell System is a novel, point-of-care electroencephalography (“EEG”) platform specifically designed to address the unmet needs of patients in the acute care setting, and is being used in hundreds of community hospitals, large academic facilities and major IDN's across the country. Our entire team is driven by a shared commitment to transforming the landscape of critical care through our rapid seizure detection technology, come join the movement!

The Sr. Manager of Commercial Strategy & Operations is an individual contributor who is a core strategic, operational, and analytical partner to Ceribell's commercial leadership team. Partnering directly with VPs, Regional Directors, Territory Managers, and Health System leaders across territories, this individual will drive forecasting, territory design, and capacity models, while establishing operational KPIs, dashboards, and strategic performance metrics to guide executive decision-making and accelerate commercial execution.

Capacity Planning & Forecasting

• Build and maintain the quarterly capacity and PO forecasting model across Territory Managers, Strategic Account Managers, and National Health Systems, reconciling bottoms-up field input with top-down company targets

Territory Strategy & Organizational Design

Pipeline Health & Funnel Analytics

Performance Diagnostics & Executive Insights

jobs.title: Staff Service Systems Engineer

jobs.description:
Company Overview

Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.

We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.

And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.

We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.

Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.

Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.

Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.

With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.

Join us in building the power foundation of the future!

Role Summary

Amperesand is deploying solid-state transformer (SST) technology into data centres and other critical sites. As our fleet grows, we need the systems and data foundations to service it at scale. We are hiring a Staff Service Systems Engineer to build them: a single, trusted service record for every unit, and the tools, processes and monitoring that keep our fleet reliable and our customers confident.

You will own the service technology stack end to end – ticketing and field service management, unit genealogy (as-built and as-maintained records), the Failure Reporting, Analysis and Corrective Action System (FRACAS), staged firmware rollout, and the design of a Network Operations Centre (NOC) that scales with the fleet. Every ticket, site visit, RMA and firmware change will connect to one unit history, so field failures link directly to Engineering, root causes are found fast, and warranty costs fall.

This is a Staff-level role with broad organisational impact. You will lead a small, growing service systems/NOC team and partner closely with firmware, software, power electronics, hardware, manufacturing and field service engineers. It suits a hands-on builder from a computer or data science background who loves diving deep into telemetry to diagnose problems, thrives in a startup, and is driven by outcomes rather than hours.

What You'll do

Responsibilities

• Own the service record: Design and implement one service record per unit, linking tickets, site visits, RMAs, configuration and firmware history across the fleet.

• Build the field service platform: Partner with the software team to design and build our own in-house ticketing and field service platform, defining requirements, data models and workflows, and integrating it with PLM/ERP, telemetry and engineering systems.

• Deliver unit genealogy: Establish as-built and as-maintained genealogy for every unit, down to serialised assemblies, so any unit’s full history is traceable in minutes.

• Own FRACAS: Build and run the FRACAS process and tooling that links field failures to Engineering, drives root-cause and corrective action, and measurably reduces warranty cost and repeat failures.

• Drive staged firmware rollout: Partner with firmware and software teams to design and operate staged, safe over-the-air rollouts with fleet cohorts, health gates, monitoring and rollback.

• Design and lead the NOC: Design NOC processes, alerting, dashboards, on-call and escalation paths that scale with the fleet; hire and lead a small team to run them.

• Deep-dive diagnostics: Use telemetry and field data to investigate and diagnose complex unit and fleet issues, respond quickly to customer-impacting events and turn findings into fixes.

• Be a hands-on generalist: Contribute wherever needed in a startup environment – including site support, data analysis, reporting and process design.

What You’ll Bring

Required Qualifications

• Years of experience: 8+ years in service systems, reliability, fleet/asset monitoring, NOC or field data engineering roles, including hands-on monitoring of assets deployed in the field.

• Education: BSc in Computer Science, Data Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Domain expertise: Deep understanding of telemetry, fleet monitoring and incident response; experience building ticketing, FRACAS, genealogy/traceability or OTA update systems.

• Leadership: Experience leading or mentoring a small team and setting technical and process standards.

• Industry experience: Energy, power electronics, data centre, industrial IoT, EV/charging, or other connected hardware fleets preferred.

• Flexibility: Willingness to travel 10–25%, including occasional multi-week deployments, and to work extended hours when fleet or customer issues demand.

• Collaboration: A team player who works well with software, electrical and hardware engineers and communicates clearly with customers.

Technical Skills

• Strong programming skills in Python; SQL and data modelling

• Telemetry and time-series data stacks (e.g. InfluxDB, TimescaleDB, Grafana) on AWS or Azure

• Experience defining requirements for, or building, internal ticketing and field service tools

• PLM/ERP systems (e.g. Arena, NetSuite) for genealogy, BOM and RMA traceability

• Designing and building staged OTA firmware rollout pipelines (familiarity with tools such as Mender or AWS IoT a plus)

• Jira (advanced), including workflow design and integrations

• Alerting, observability and incident management practices; APIs and system integration

Nice to Have

• Startup or early-stage hardware company experience

• Reliability engineering background (FMEA, Weibull analysis, MTBF)

• Experience setting up a NOC or 24/7 monitoring operation from scratch

• Familiarity with industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, IEC 61850) and SCADA/BMS integration

• Knowledge of power electronics or MV equipment

• Cloud or ITIL certifications

Working Model

Employment Type:
• Full-time

Location:
[San Francisco/Sunnyvale / Reno ]

Work Model:
• Onsite

Travel Requirements:
10%-25%

Onsite Collaboration Rationale:
Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.

Why Join Amperesand

• Work on next-generation power infrastructure systems • High ownership and visibility • Cross-functional collaboration • Opportunity to shape future products and infrastructure • Fast-moving startup environment

Please note: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options.

While this role is listed for the location above, we may consider candidates in other locations on a case-by-case basis.

Onsite Collaboration Rationale:

Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.

Why Join Amperesand

Pay Disclosure & Benefits

Additional benefits may be available depending on the role and employment type. Benefits are subject to the terms of applicable company policies and plans.

Candidate Confidentiality & Information Protection

As part of our commitment to protecting confidential and proprietary information, candidates should not disclose or provide Amperesand with any confidential, proprietary, or trade secret information belonging to a current or former employer or any other third party during the application or interview process.

jobs.title: Senior Thermal Engineer
jobs.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

As a Senior Thermal Engineer, you will serve as the technical authority for Divergent’s aero-structures portfolio, responsible for pushing the envelope of our technology with respect to thermal optimization and performance of Divergent’s structural components. You’ll be accountable for owning the full development life cycle from conceptual design through customer delivery, ensuring high-performance, reliable systems that meet the demands of complex, unforgiving environments.

This role demands both technical depth and program maturity: the ability to engage government and industry partners to refine requirements for thermal performance for both new and legacy systems, while fostering internal alignment across internal engineering teams. You will be called on to derive thermal requirements in the absence of written specifications and are expected to challenge and shape requirements when appropriate — ensuring that the final product meets mission intent.

The Role

• Serve as the thermal design authority for Divergent’s A&D Structures team, owning thermal architecture from concept through qualification.

• Define, negotiate, and validate thermal requirements and budgets with government and industry customers.

• Develop thermal management strategies and lead internal trade studies—including heat rejection, insulation, and material selection.

• Guide thermal aspects of design reviews, establish standardized thermal maturity metrics and qualification criteria across Divergent’s A&D customer portfolio.

• Build and maintain high-fidelity thermal models (conduction, convection, radiation, steady state and transient analyses) and drive correlation with test data throughout the product lifecycle. Accountable for comprehensive thermal qualification and verification planning, including environmental testing, thermal cycling, and thermal analysis correlation.

• Collaborate with senior technical experts to establish thermal analysis standards and model technical excellence inside and outside the organization, including with government customers and prime contractors.

• Support vehicle builds and product development testing, including thermal instrumentation, data reduction, and troubleshooting.

• Collaborates with senior technical experts to establish technical standards, and models technical excellence inside and outside the organization including government customers and prime contractors.

Basic Qualifications:

• Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline with a thermal sciences focus.

• Minimum 8 years of experience in thermal analysis, design, or management.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to synthesize complex thermal development engineering to simple terms and find alignment across multifunctional stakeholders including government customers and prime contractors.

• Strong analytical and practical mindset—comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving structured clarity across thermal, structural, and systems boundaries.

• Demonstrated excellence in thermal requirements definition, verification planning, and risk management across terrestrial & space thermal development and multidisciplinary teams.

• Experience interfacing with engineering, testing, and manufacturing groups to understand system designs and the associated thermal constraints.

• Demonstrated expertise in thermal analysis throughout the design, build, and test phases of a development cycle, including steady-state and transient modeling.

• Proficiency with industry thermal analysis tools such as ANSYS (Fluent, Thermal Desktop, Icepak), Star CCM+, PowerFlow.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Current Secret DoD security clearance or ability to obtain and retain clearance within 365 days from submission.

• 8+ years of experience in a broad range of terrestrial and space system development applications and qualification.

• Familiarity with relevant MIL-STDs (e.g., MIL-STD-810 thermal methods, MIL-STD-1540 environmental testing) and NASA STD’s (e.g., NASA-STD-7002 – Thermal Verification, KSC-STD-Z-0017). Proficiency in NASA-ST-6030 - Additive Manufacturing Requirements for Spaceflight Systems preferred.

• Demonstrated excellence in developing thermal solutions for aerospace and defense applications, including aerodynamic heating, electronics cooling, and propulsion thermal management.

• Experience with additive manufacturing, advanced thermal interface materials, or novel cooling architectures.

• Expert understanding of thermophysical properties and thermal behavior of various material systems (composites, adhesives, metals) across operational temperature ranges.

• Experience with thermal vacuum testing, altitude simulation, and correlation of thermal models to test data.

Work Environment

• Requires frequent standing, walking, and interaction across production and R&D work areas.

• May occasionally require extended or weekend hours to meet production deadlines.

• Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment and keyboards.

Compensation

At Divergent, our pay range is based on the level of the job.  For this role, we will consider candidates at level E05 as evaluated through our interview process

• E05 / Senior: $141,380 - $194,390

Pay Range

$141,380—$194,390 USD

What We Offer Our Regular, Full-Time Employees:

• Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.

• Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.

• Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.

• Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.

• Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.

Divergent provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.

jobs.title: Solutions Engineer, AI Data
jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW

Most companies don’t end in acquisition — they end in closure. Yet shutdown has never been given the same rigor, clarity, or professionalism as the moments that came before it. Nearly 4 million companies shut down every year, creating a massive, overlooked market. SimpleClosure is building the infrastructure to change that.

Having raised over $20M from leading VCs and trusted by more than 7,000 companies to date, we streamline the entire business dissolution process — from legal and tax to operational and administrative — as one coordinated effort instead of a patchwork of disconnected steps. We go a step further, helping companies sell their remaining assets and return the most value to their stakeholders, through our Asset Hub.

As the leading platform for company shutdowns, we have something no one else does: a continuous, proprietary flow of companies winding down, and the assets they built along the way. Our buyers span the top AI labs, RL environment providers, vertical and enterprise agent builders, VCs and deal-flow partners, domain marketplaces, and much more. Dissolution is our wedge; the marketplace is a big part of where we’re headed.

Joining our Asset Hub team means helping to define a new category from the ground up, working on complex, high-stakes problems, and building the products and processes that guide founders through one of the most consequential moments in a company’s life.


JOB OVERVIEW

SimpleClosure is seeking a Solutions Engineer, AI Data, to own how AssetHub’s data gets from the companies that built it into the hands of the AI labs that buy it. When companies wind down, we acquire the real assets they built — production codebases, workspaces, and databases. You’ll pull that data from sellers, shape it to each buyer’s exact requirements, deliver it, and work with buyers to implement different feedback or fixes.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing engineering role that could be forward deployed in some instances. You’ll work directly with research and data teams at frontier AI labs and with founders and engineers on the seller side, in a small, dedicated Asset Hub pod alongside product, engineering, BD, and the GM of Asset Hub.

*Candidates MUST be located in the New York City Metro area.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Work with sellers and their engineers to extract codebases, workspace exports (Slack, Jira, Notion, Drive), and databases, and ingest them cleanly into our pipeline.

 - Translate each buyer’s requirements into custom scripts: transformations, filters, formats, and packaging tailored to how they train and evaluate models.

 - Own technical delivery end to end: delivery specs, secure transfer, documentation, validation, and iteration until the buyer confirms the data is usable.

 - Build and run evaluation scripts on codebases and workspaces (quality, completeness, size, training and RL signal), and help define how AssetHub scores and prices assets.

 - Be the technical point of contact for lab data teams: join buyer calls, answer technical questions, scope custom requests, and feed what you learn into product and pricing.

 - Turn one-off scripts into reusable tooling so every delivery is faster than the last.

 - Handle sensitive material (codebases, workspace exports, and proprietary datasets) with strong attention to security, privacy, licensing, and PII handling.


DESIRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience: 2–5 years as a software, data, or ML engineer, ideally in a forward deployed, solutions, or other customer-facing engineering role.

 - Core engineering: strong Python and SQL; fast, production-quality scripting and data pipelines; comfortable with messy real-world data.

 - Evals: familiarity with how LLMs are trained and evaluated, including pretraining vs. SFT vs. RL data, evals, agent harnesses, and RL environments.

 - Ownership: takes delivery from first request to accepted dataset, works scrappily, and thrives in ambiguity.

 - Communication: credible with a lab researcher in the morning and a seller’s founder in the afternoon.

 - Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Nice to have - AI-data / evaluation background: experience at an AI data vendor (e.g. Scale, Surge, Snorkel, Mercor, Handshake AI, Turing) or on a lab’s data team, or hands-on work producing training or evaluation data for models. Data licensing or compliance exposure; contributions to public benchmarks or eval frameworks.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Compensation: $140,000 to $170,000

 - Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision

 - Life insurance

 - Unlimited paid time off

 - Flexible hybrid work environment in New York City, Midtown (currently 2 days per week in office)

 - Two company-wide offsites each year

 - 401(k) with Traditional and Roth options, with immediate eligibility


SIMPLECLOSURE IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

We are committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions at SimpleClosure — including recruiting, hiring, promotion, compensation, and termination — are based on qualifications, merit, and business need, without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please let us know.


APPLICATION PROCESS

Thanks for applying! If your experience is a strong match for what we’re looking for, our hiring team will reach out to schedule an initial screening call and walk you through the rest of our interview process. We do our best to respond to every applicant, but given the volume of applications we receive, we may not be able to provide individual updates if we decide not to move forward.
