jobs.title: Electrical Test Specialist, Intelligence Systems
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The production test team is responsible for building, testing, and delivering defense-critical hardware for Intelligence Systems programs. The team designs and deploys test systems to the production lines that assemble and integrate complex electronic systems into products that ship to the customer.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for an Electrical Test Specialist to join our rapidly growing production test team. WHAT YOU'LL DO

jobs.title: Senior Hydrodynamics Engineer
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Senior Hydrodynamics Engineer, you will lead the design, analysis, test, and certification of the Seaglider hydrofoil system. You will draw on analytical, empirical, and advanced computational methods to develop models of hull-sailing, hydrofoiling, takeoff, and landing. You will use these models to analyze vehicle dynamics, stability, and control, and to set operating limitations.

Many of these problems are highly coupled. You will know how to simplify them, when to apply deeper analytical rigor, and how to arrive at the most cost-effective solution, and then you'll test to prove it works.

As part of the Vehicle Sciences team, you'll join a group of driven, collaborative engineers who hold a high bar, move quickly, and think boldly to bring entirely new technology into the world.

If you're energized by working at the intersection of cutting-edge innovation, real-world impact, and hands-on engineering, you'll be in the right place, and we'd be thrilled to have you on the team!




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Conduct Hydrodynamic Analyses: Run and interpret free-surface CFD for float, takeoff, foiling, and touchdown, including ventilation, cavitation, spray, and hull impact.

 - Define the Operational Envelope: Establish the conditions and limits within which the vehicle can safely float, take off, foil, and land, based on analysis and test data.

 - Build the Models for the Simulator: Turn CFD and test results into reduced-order models, such as force and moment databases and ventilation and impact models, that feed our vehicle simulator.

 - Evaluate Stability and Controllability on the Water: Assess how the vehicle behaves and responds to control inputs across the water envelope, and work with the controls team to carry the findings into control law development.

 - Shape the Hydrofoil and Hull Design: Leverage lower order methods (vortex lattice, lifting line) and lead foil and strut trades on sizing, placement, planform, and airfoil.

 - Support Loads Evaluation: Provide hydrodynamic pressure distributions and loads for hull, foil, and strut sizing, documented for design reviews and certification.

 - Run the Toolchain: Build and maintain our hydrodynamic design and analysis tools, from low-fidelity foil design to CFD workflows, and cross-check them against each other.

 - Correlate Analysis to Test: Define validation objectives for tow-tank, sub-scale, and full-scale on-water tests, work with flight test on instrumentation, and calibrate models against measured vehicle dynamics.

 - Grow the Team: Mentor junior engineers and break large analysis problems into well-bounded tasks.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Multiphase CFD: Expert with a commercial or open-source free-surface solver, including meshing, turbulence and multiphase modeling choices, and solution verification.

 - Validation: You have compared CFD to experiment on a real vehicle, found where it was wrong, and fixed the model. You know the difference between converged and correct.

 - Model Building: You have built reduced-order models from high-fidelity results that a simulation or controls team used.

 - Lifting Surfaces: Solid grounding in foil hydrodynamics, and working knowledge of low- and mid-fidelity tools (panel, lifting-line, vortex-lattice), with the judgment to know when they suffice and when CFD is needed.

 - Automation: Strong Python or MATLAB scripting on Linux/HPC. You automate geometry, meshing, and post-processing rather than click through them.

 - Experiments: You have designed or run validation experiments (tow tank, wind tunnel, or on-vehicle test) and worked with real instrumentation data.

 - Experience: Ideally M.S. or Ph.D. in Aerospace, Mechanical, Ocean, or Naval Engineering (or equivalent), with industry experience of applied fluid dynamics experience beyond the degree.

 - Mentorship: Experience developing junior engineers or students.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively with structures, controls, test, and design engineers, and you make sure your results land in a form the next team can use.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex physics with incomplete data. Whether it's a ventilated foil touchdown or a hull slamming into a wave, you find the right fidelity for the question and get to a defensible answer.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you move between hydro CFD, hand calculations, simulator modeling, and test support as priorities shift, and you keep progress going without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for building things that haven't existed before. You continuously improve the team's tools, workflows, and standards for verification.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation including a robust equity incentive plan.

 - Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance - we cover 100% of your premiums.

 - 401(k) with company matching, so you can plan for the future.

 - Generous flexible time off, paid parental leave, and company-wide holiday breaks.

 - Relocation packages available for those moving to join our team.

 - Daily, free catered lunches

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

jobs.title: AI Ops Engineer (GTM)
jobs.description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.



Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.



Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.



A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.



🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.



 💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.



🤝  We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.



💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.



The Role 🔭

We're rebuilding Orbital's go-to-market around AI. Not by adding another tool to the stack, but by rethinking how we find, win and grow customers from first principles.

As an AI Ops Engineer (GTM) on our Revenue team, you'll sit with the people doing the work across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Finance. You'll question how we work today, reimagine it from first principles with AI, and build what replaces it. You're essentially an internal forward deployed engineer. Over time, you'll help join up the whole business so every team works off the same data and foundations.

The technology is changing every month. We want someone who finds new and unusual ways of doing things, and builds them so they keep working as the tools change.

You'll report to the VP of RevOps. This role is for someone early in their career with exceptional raw ability: we care far more about how fast you learn and what you've built than about years of experience or job titles.



What you'll do 🎯

 - Embed with revenue teams to understand how they work, and spot where AI and automation could change the outcome

 - Connect our systems (CRM, marketing, CS, product and finance data) so teams work from one trusted picture of the customer

 - Try new approaches, test them quickly with real users, and keep what works

 - Ship in short cycles and prove impact. Build the measures that show pipeline created, conversion lift and time saved

 - Build things to last: documented, maintainable and easy to adapt as models and tools change

 - Share what you learn and help colleagues get more out of AI
   
   

What you'll bring 💡

Nice to have

 - Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing startup

As Principal Software Engineer & Architect, you will own the technical direction of the data and platform systems behind detection, investigation, hunting, response, and AI-driven defense. Several engineering teams will build against your architecture, and your decisions will show up in measurable security outcomes.

What You'll Do

• Own the architecture of our multi-system security data platform, from ingestion to access, including the data that powers detection, investigation, hunting and risk analytics. Decide what data lives where, weighing business value, performance, retention, and cost, and remove duplication across systems.

jobs.title: Materials Engineer (Metals)
jobs.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler  (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber’s first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

About The Role:

We are seeking a curious, hands-on materials engineer to help develop and integrate materials and processes into market-defining commercial devices. You will apply materials science fundamentals to understand how processing affects the structure and properties of metals and ceramics, working alongside experienced engineers to develop processes that meet device requirements.

Your work will span materials processing, characterization, and property testing, with opportunities to build experience in heat treatment, thin-film deposition, bonding, and other fabrication techniques. You will help evaluate incoming materials, investigate how processing changes their behavior, and use experimental results to improve process consistency and performance. You will also collaborate with adjacent teams to transfer established processes from our prototyping fab to our digital, autonomous manufacturing platform.

This full-time position is based in our Emeryville site within the Process Engineering organization.

What You’ll Do:

• Plan and execute experiments with guidance appropriate to experience to understand processing–structure–property relationships across a range of materials, with a focus on metals and ceramics.

• Own assigned process development tasks and projects, troubleshoot issues, and contribute improvements to procedures and tool capabilities.

• Operate materials processing equipment for applications such as rolling, forming, alloy heat treatment, thin-film deposition, and bonding.

• Apply bulk and surface characterization techniques to evaluate materials and monitor process outputs.

• Help evaluate incoming materials through supplier documentation review and in-house testing, and contribute to refining material specifications.

• Collaborate with engineers, technicians, and operators to develop processes and transfer materials, procedures, and supporting documentation into fabrication workflows.

• Follow established processing and safety protocols, analyze experimental data, document procedures, maintain accurate records, and communicate key findings.

What You’ll Need:

• Bachelor’s degree in Materials Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related field, with 2–3 years of relevant experience, including research or internships.

• Working knowledge of physical metallurgy and processing–structure–property relationships in metals and alloys.

• Hands-on experience processing or characterizing metals, alloys, or coatings.

• Experience with one or more materials characterization techniques (e.g., metallography, SEM, EDS, EBSD, XRF, XRD) or material property tests (e.g., tensile, hardness, fatigue, micro- or nanoindentation).

• Ability to plan systematic experiments, interpret results critically, and communicate findings clearly.

The compensation for this position also includes equity and benefits.

$140,000—$170,000 USD

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Accounts Payable - Payments
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Procurement team makes working with the world easy, fast, and safe. We connect supplier readiness, purchasing, invoicing, and payment so teams can move with confidence as OpenAI scales. Accounts Payable provides the trusted data, dependable execution, and financial discipline behind that experience.



About the Role

We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Senior Manager to own and scale supplier payment operations. You’ll be responsible for accurate, timely payments, strong controls, and dependable service as OpenAI grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You’ll review and approve supplier payment runs, oversee work initiated by our BPO teams and AP agents, as well as personally resolve complex exceptions. You’ll stay close to execution during volume spikes and month-end close while building the processes, coverage, and systems the team needs to scale.

You’ll partner with Procurement, Supplier Master Data Operations, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Finance Systems, and existing AP processing teams to make payments reliable from payment readiness through settlement reconciliation. You’ll clarify handoffs, address recurring failures, and improve ERP, banking, and procurement workflows. You’ll also apply automation and AI where they improve accuracy, service, or team capacity, with appropriate controls and human review.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office (Mon-Wed) per week and we offer relocation assistance to new employees.



We’re looking for someone with:

 - Strategic AP leadership and a hands-on approach to scaling systems and processes, with strong attention to detail.

 - Demonstrated ownership of complex indirect AP and supplier-payment operations, including PO and non-PO workflows.

 - Experience leading teams or outsourced delivery partners, setting expectations, developing capability, and managing performance.

 - Strong payment-control judgment and experience investigating duplicates, bank-detail changes, and payment failures.

 - Working depth in AP accounting, reconciliations, accrual inputs, and close coordination.

 - Experience translating AP needs into ERP or procurement-system improvements with measurable results.

 - Clear communication and the ability to influence partners and senior stakeholders in ambiguous situations.



In this role, you will:

 - Own supplier payment operations: Review and approve payment runs for supplier and payment data accuracy, required approvals, and exception resolution. Oversee manual disbursements and payment inquiries within established authority and segregation-of-duties requirements.

 - Resolve complex exceptions: Act as the primary escalation point for payment holds, rejected or returned payments, potential duplicates, and close blockers. Work with Treasury, banking partners, Accounting, and AP processing teams to establish the status, resolve the cause, and verify the outcome before retrying or closing an issue.

 - Strengthen payment readiness: Partner with Procurement and existing AP teams to resolve invoice, PO, approval, and supplier-data gaps that affect payment. Establish clear owners and follow through on recurring upstream issues.

 - Support forecasting and close: Provide reliable payment forecasts and cash-needs inputs to Treasury. Reconcile payment activity and exceptions, including payments after AP close, so Accounting has the evidence it needs for close and cutoff decisions.

 - Maintain effective controls: Uphold SOX-aligned approvals, independent supplier bank-detail verification, segregation of duties, and audit-ready documentation. Support internal and external audits and remediate control gaps with the relevant owners.

 - Improve systems and processes: Define payment workflow and reporting requirements with Finance Systems and other partners. Test ERP and bank integrations, including host-to-host workflows, and introduce automation or AI with validated outputs, exception handling, and clear accountability.

 - Lead BPO delivery and capacity: Set clear SLAs and KPIs, review quality and performance, coach service partners, and maintain documented procedures and backup coverage. Plan for volume spikes and close demands.

 - Report performance and risk: Own clear reporting on payment timeliness, exceptions, rejection and return trends, forecast accuracy, service quality, and control issues. Explain priorities and progress to stakeholders and leadership.



You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Bring 8+ years in AP, payments, or related finance operations, or equivalent experience, with personal ownership of complex supplier-payment operations and material exceptions.

 - Have worked across indirect supplier spend in a high-growth or scaling environment, balancing immediate delivery with durable process improvements.

 - Understand how invoices, approvals, supplier records, payment instructions, bank status, settlement, and reconciliation fit together, and can investigate discrepancies across them.

 - Bring a strong controls mindset aligned to SOX, including practical judgment on bank-detail changes, duplicate prevention, segregation of duties, reconciliation, and close support.

 - Have designed or improved ERP/AP payment workflows and bank integrations, including host-to-host automation, with tested controls and measurable results.

 - Have led teams or BPO partners through clear expectations, coaching, capacity planning, and sustained improvements in service and quality.

 - Communicate clearly with suppliers, business stakeholders, and senior leaders, and can resolve issues across teams without losing ownership.

 - Are willing to work directly in payment queues, investigate failures, and support close when needed.

 - Experience with Oracle Fusion, Zip, or comparable integrated finance systems, and practical use of AI in controlled finance workflows, would be helpful.

Sitting

Lifting

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Access to insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

You must be 16 years of age or older.

General job duties for all store team members

• Operate all equipment.
• Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
• Prepare product.
• Receive and process telephone orders.
• Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
• Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.
• Expedite carryout and delivery orders to vehicles.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the

phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

• Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
• Must be able to make correct monetary change.
• Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
• Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
• Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to:

• Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
• In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
• Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
• Fumes from food odors.
• Exposure to cornmeal dust.
• Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
• Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
• Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

• Talking and hearing on telephone.
• Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
• Depth perception.
• Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing: Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking: For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

• Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
• Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
• Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

• Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
• Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
• Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

• To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24"- 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
• Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

• Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
• Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
• Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
• Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

• Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
• Workers reach above 72"occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
• Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
• Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

• Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
• Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
• Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
• Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
• Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
• Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Team

OKX’s Global Legal team provides strategic legal, regulatory, and policy guidance to OKX and its affiliated entities across jurisdictions and business lines. The team partners closely with stakeholders across Compliance, Product, Communications, Operations, and the broader business to support responsible growth in a rapidly evolving global regulatory environment.

We are a collaborative, high-performing, and fast-paced team that values practical judgment, intellectual curiosity, and clear communication. Our global team of more than 60 lawyers works across multiple regions, with the Chief Legal Officer based in the United States.

About the Role

We are seeking a Government Relations & Public Policy Manager to support OKX’s engagement with U.S. policymakers, regulators, industry stakeholders, and external advocacy partners. This is a high-visibility, execution-oriented role at the intersection of policy, regulation, licensing, and business strategy.

Reporting to a senior member of the Legal Department and working closely with external advisors including lobbying, policy, and legal partners, you will help advance OKX’s U.S. policy and regulatory priorities across federal and, where relevant, state-level issues affecting crypto and digital assets. You will translate regulatory developments into practical insights, coordinate external engagement, and work cross-functionally to ensure policy considerations are reflected in business decisions.

This role is well suited to a thoughtful, highly organized policy professional who is ready to build depth in digital-assets regulation and take increasing ownership of key workstreams.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Support the development and execution of OKX’s U.S. government relations and public-policy strategy.

• Monitor and analyze federal and state legislative, regulatory, and political developments relevant to crypto, financial services, market structure, consumer protection, AML, sanctions, and technology.

• Distill complex policy and regulatory developments into clear, actionable briefings for Legal, Compliance, Product, Communications, and business teams.

• Help prepare regulatory submissions, consultation responses, policy memos, comment letters, and other external-facing materials.

• Partner closely with external lobbying firms to coordinate advocacy priorities, meeting preparation, intelligence gathering, and follow-up across federal and state policy workstreams.

• Manage day-to-day engagement with relevant trade associations, coalitions, and industry working groups; identify opportunities to advance OKX’s policy priorities.

• Represent or support OKX at policy conferences, regulatory roundtables, industry events, and other external forums.

• Support the company’s PAC advisory activities, including policy research, stakeholder mapping, meeting preparation, and administration in partnership with the Global CLO, Legal team, and external advisors.

• Build and maintain productive working relationships with policymakers, regulators, congressional staff, industry groups, and other external stakeholders.

• Support meetings involving senior company leaders and external stakeholders, including preparation, attendance where appropriate, follow-up, and tracking of commitments.

• Maintain organized records of external engagements, policy developments, advocacy priorities, and key commitments.

What We Look For In You

• 6+ years of relevant experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, law, financial services, or a related field.

• Familiarity with U.S. financial-services regulation and the policy issues shaping crypto and digital assets.

• Experience working with government, a regulator, Congress, a trade association, policy consultancy, law firm, lobbying firm, or a regulated financial-services or technology company.

• Strong research, analytical, writing, and presentation skills; able to make complex issues accessible to non-specialist audiences.

• Experience producing polished meeting materials, stakeholder briefings, policy memos, and presentations under tight deadlines.

• Excellent project-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and maintain close attention to detail.

• Sound judgment, discretion, and a collaborative approach to working across functions.

• Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where policy and business priorities can evolve quickly.

• A genuine interest in the future of digital assets, financial innovation, and responsible regulation.

Nice to Haves

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the

phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTSincluding, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile"bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72"high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24"- 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72"occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing"walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

You want to be the boss? Well now's your chance – Domino's Pizza is hiring bosses – more specifically assistant managers. It's a tough job, one that needs a natural like you. Of course, you'll need some skills – judgment, math and the ability to multitask.

You'll be working for a company that's fun and flexible. Not to mention, it's work experience you're going to use for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now help us be the best in pizza delivery. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

JOB REQUIREMENTS AND DUTIES

You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and Customer relations. You must set the example. You must follow ALL policy and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew.

In addition: Staffing, Paperwork, Cost Controls, Cash control, Food management, Work to a Schedule, Perfect Image and adherence to standards, Great Customer Service, Attendance & punctuality, Transportation to/from work, Store cleanliness, Marketing, Profitability.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From delivery driver to management, general manager to franchisee or Manager Corporate Operations, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

QUALIFICATIONS

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Prepare product.

Receive and process telephone orders.

Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).

Must be able to make correct monetary change.

Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.

Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.

Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

Fumes from food odors.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.

Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception.

Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.

Surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 – 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

DRIVING SPECIFIC JOB DUTIES

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

REQUIRES

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to an insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS

Navigational skills to read a map, locate addresses within designated delivery area.

Must navigate adverse terrain including multi-story buildings, private homes, and other delivery sites while carrying product.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Carrying

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Walking

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Climbing

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure To

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when delivering product, driving and couponing.

SENSING

Far vision and night vision for driving.

jobs.title: Commercial Activation Lead
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic funds delivery partners to help customers adopt Claude, through assessments, workshops, proofs of concept, and full delivery engagements. Our partner request process is the front door for all of it: an account executive (AE) requests partner support, and the request is checked against program rules and matched to a partner.

Commercial is the program's highest-volume segment, and the one where a quick introduction and the right match matter most. Automation now drafts the first match and the introduction, and a vendor delivery team handles day-to-day follow-up and tracker updates. What's left is the work that needs a person sellers trust.

You'll be the one Activations contact for US Commercial sellers once a request is in, from submission to a partner on a signed statement of work (SOW). Partner Sales Managers (PSMs) attach the partner and own the opportunity, and at their volume they move on to the next deal. You'll own the follow-through: matching and re-matching, getting AE and customer introductions to happen, handling exception requests, and working the special cases that don't fit the standard path. Decision rights are clear: the program lead sets program rules, targets, and exception policy; you apply them on Commercial requests, decide what the rules already cover, and bring the rest with a recommendation.

We're looking for a partner seller or channel operator whom sellers and partners trust, who is comfortable owning a high-volume book, and who keeps following up until each request is closed. Success in this role comes down to three things: how quickly Commercial requests move from AE introduction to customer introduction and on to a signed SOW, whether sellers know exactly who to go to and get a straight answer, and whether exceptions are handled the same way every time.

Key responsibilities

• Serve as the single point of contact for the AE, the PSM, and the partner on every US Commercial request, from submission to confirmed SOW, so sellers deal with one person instead of several

• Answer "Where is my request?" with the current status, the blocker, and the next step with a date, and keep each request's record accurate enough that the answer is already written down

• Join the PSM pipeline and activation calls every week so requests don't slip between PSMs, and leave each call with an owner and a date on every open Commercial request discussed

• Own the request and its follow-through within clear boundaries: the PSM owns the opportunity, partner attach, and getting the SOW signed; the partner manager owns the partner relationship; and you hand over cleanly to Partner Success once the SOW is confirmed

• Confirm the first match that automation drafts from the partner bench, change it when it's wrong for the customer, and own the matching decision on Commercial requests; check that a partner has capacity before introductions go out, and spread work so no partner holds more open introductions than it can take

• Re-match quickly when a partner declines, stalls, or is turned down by the AE, record the reason, and make sure the request has an owner in between

• Review where Commercial matches are declined or lost, and turn repeat causes into changes to the matching rules

• Follow up on automatically drafted introductions that an AE hasn't approved, and resolve what the escalation rules send to you; step in when a partner's booking of the customer introduction stalls, and work with the AE or their manager to unblock it

• Run the regular review of aged Commercial requests, making sure each one has a recorded decision (introduction made, customer not ready, re-match, or close out) and a follow-up date

• Track every Commercial request from partner named to confirmed SOW, publish the baseline for that stage, and remove the blockers that sit with Anthropic

• Be the first stop for Commercial exception requests, including special order-form terms: resolve what the rules already cover, bring the rest to the program lead with the history, the blocker, and a recommended action, and log every exception consistently so approvals follow the agreed routing and can be audited later

• Work through cases the standard path doesn't fit, such as small and medium business (SMB), insurance, and other segment-specific use cases, and write down how each type is handled so the next one is faster

• Run tests of new funding programs, which start in Commercial, with sellers and partners, and report back what worked, what confused people, and what should change before a wider launch

• Teach Commercial AEs and their managers how to request a partner, how one-click introductions work, and what the response rules are, so requests arrive complete the first time; make sure PSMs and partner managers know the stage targets, who to contact once a request is in, and how escalations work

• Work with the activation systems and operations lead to turn repeat exceptions and repeat questions into rule changes or automation, so fewer requests need a person each quarter

• Use Claude to prepare for pipeline calls, draft follow-ups, and summarize the state of your book, and propose the next manual step worth automating

• Work US hours with a regular overlap window with the London-based program lead, and hand off cleanly so Commercial sellers have coverage across time zones

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in partner sales, channel, or partner operations in B2B technology

• Experience working with services partners or systems integrators: matching them to customer work, judging fit and capacity, and holding them to commitments

• Experience working alongside AEs and sales managers on live deals, and able to get a response from a busy AE while keeping the relationship strong

• Sound judgment on exceptions: knows the difference between a case the rules already cover and one that needs a decision, and makes a clear recommendation on the second kind

• Persistent, courteous follow-through with internal and external stakeholders, and doesn't let items slip past their deadline

• Clear, concise writing: short messages people act on, and escalations that give the facts, the ask, and a recommendation

• Comfortable with ambiguity and rules that change often: asks good questions, writes the answer down, and applies it consistently

• Works comfortably with records and reports in Salesforce

• Uses Claude or similar AI tools in day-to-day work

Preferred qualifications

• Experience as a Partner Sales Manager or in a closely related role

• Experience using Claude specifically in day-to-day work

• Experience with partner funding, market development funds (MDF), or co-sell programs

• Experience with order forms and SOW workflows

• Experience selling into SMB or insurance

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$170,000—$215,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

· Operate all equipment.

· Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

· Prepare product.

· Receive and process telephone orders.

· Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.

· Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

· Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.

· Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

· Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.

· In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

· Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.

· Fumes from food odors.

· Exposure to cornmeal dust.

· Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.

· Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

· Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

· Talking and hearing on telephone. Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.

· Depth perception.

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 4".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table

Lifting

· Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.

· Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

· Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

· Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.

· Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

· Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

· To move trays which are placed on dollies.

· A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

· Trays may also be pulled.

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

· Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

· Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

· Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

· Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

· Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

· Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

· Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

· Frequently activities require use of one or both hands. Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

· Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.

· Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

· Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Verbal, writing, and telephone communication skills to take and process orders.

Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions.

In-store temperatures ranging from 33 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.

Sudden changes in temperature in the work area and while outside.

Fumes from artificial and natural scents or odors from food, gases, air fresheners, etc.

Exposure to cornmeal dust.

Confined spaces, such as a walk-in cooler.

Hot surfaces, tools, and products from the oven up to 500 degrees or higher.

Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

REQUIRED MENTAL AND PHYSICAL ABILITIES (Including, but not limited to the following):

SENSING

The ability to speak, hear, and understand verbal communication on telephone and in person is necessary.

Near and mid-range vision is used for most in-store tasks.

Depth perception in necessary for all positions.

Personnel must have the ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

Far vision and night vision are needed for delivery personnel.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgments and decisions is necessary throughout shifts.

STANDING

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking surfaces include ceramic tile, concrete, or linoleum in some food process areas.

Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

WALKING

Walking is frequently required for short distances and short durations.

Personnel must travel between the store and customer vehicles.

Delivery personnel must travel between delivery vehicles/e-bikes and from the delivery vehicle/e-bike to the customer's location.

SITTING

Paperwork is normally completed while sitting.

Driving to and from deliveries or meetings requires sitting.

LIFTING

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team members on duty during the deliveries.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from the floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

CARRYING

Dough trays weigh approximately 12 pounds, cases of products weighing up to 25 pounds, and prepped items may need to be carried from the walk-in cooler to the make-line.

Items such as cases of pizza sauce, weighing 30 pounds, may occasionally need to be carried from the storage area to the prep area, and from the prep area to the front of the store.

During delivery, carrying products while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties may be required.

PUSHING/PULLING

This may be required to move trays or products placed on dollies, or to move empty trays or trash cans.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

CLIMBING

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change air fresheners, clean walls, or perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

BENDING/CROUCHING/SQUATTING

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.

Duration of this position is generally less than one minute and may be repeated frequently.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking items.

REACHING

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven, heat lamp, or television controls, and to lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reach down to perform tasks such as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

HAND TASKS

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.

Activities frequently require use of one or both hands.

Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.

Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the different pizza cutters.

Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.

Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter, the pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

MACHINES, TOOLS, EQUIPTMENT, AND WORK AIDS

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutters, and pizza peels, and scales.

ADVANCEMENT

Many of our team members began their careers as delivery drivers and today are successful Domino's franchise owners. From customer service representative to management, General Manager to Manager Corporate Operations or Franchisee, our stores offer a world of opportunity.

DIVERSITY

Our mission is to recognize, appreciate, value and utilize the unique talents and contributions of all individuals. To create an environment where all team members, because of their differences, can reach their highest potential.

SUMMARY STATEMENT

We take pride in our team members and our team members take pride in Domino's Pizza! Being the best pizza delivery company in the world requires exceptional team members working together. At Domino's Pizza, our people come first!

JOB REQUIREMENTS

You must be 16 years of age or older.

General job duties for all store team members

Operate all equipment.
Stock ingredients from delivery area to storage, work area, walk-in cooler.
Prepare product.
Receive and process telephone orders.
Take inventory and complete associated paperwork.
Clean equipment and facility approximately daily.

Training

Orientation and training provided on the job.

Communication Skills

Ability to comprehend and give correct written instructions.
Ability to communicate verbally with customers and co-workers to process orders both over the phone and in person.

Essential Functions/Skills

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide accurately and quickly (may use calculator).
Must be able to make correct monetary change.
Verbal, writing, and telephone skills to take and process orders.
Motor coordination between eyes and hands/fingers to rapidly and accurately make precise movements with speed.
Ability to enter orders using a computer keyboard or touch screen.

WORK CONDITIONS

Exposure to:

Varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions when removing trash and performing other outside tasks.
In-store temperatures range from 36 degrees in cooler to 90 degrees and above in some work areas.
Sudden changes in temperature in work area and while outside.
Fumes from food odors.
Exposure to cornmeal dust.
Cramped quarters including walk-in cooler.
Hot surfaces/tools from oven up to 500 degrees or higher.
Sharp edges and moving mechanical parts.

SENSING

Talking and hearing on telephone.
Near and mid-range vision for most in-store tasks.
Depth perception.
Ability to differentiate between hot and cold surfaces.

TEMPERAMENTS

The ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, deal with people, analyze and compile data, make judgements and decisions.

Additional Job Details

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS including, but not limited to the following:
Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position.

Walking

For short distances for short durations.
Surfaces include ceramic tile bricks with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36 and 48.

Sitting

Paperwork is normally completed in an office at a desk or table.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made twice a week or more and are unloaded by the team member using a hand truck.
Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.
Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72 high.

Carrying

Large cans, weighing 3 pounds, 7 ounces, are carried from the workstation to storage shelves.
Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.
Trays of pizza dough are carried three at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 12 pounds per tray.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies. A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24 - 30 and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.
Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to change prices on signs, wash walls, perform maintenance.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.
Toe room is present, but workers are unable to flex their knees while standing at this station.
Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.
Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.
Workers reach above 72 occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.
Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.
Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Hand Tasks

Eye-hand coordination is essential. Use of hands is continuous during the day.
Frequently activities require use of one or both hands.
Shaping pizza dough requires frequent and forceful use of forearms and wrists.
Workers must manipulate a pizza peel when removing pizza from the oven, and when using the rolling cutter.
Frequent and/or forceful pinching is required in the assembly of cardboard pizza boxes.
Team Members must be able to grasp cans, the phone, the pizza cutter and pizza peel, and pizza boxes.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

jobs.title: General Manager In Training (02520) - 914 Eastern Blvd
jobs.description:
General Manager-In-Training

Looking for an opportunity to get ahead? Great! Now be sure to read everything until the end.  At Domino’s we provide plenty opportunities. We are not normal pizza people. We are pizza fanatics. Together we create a career and chance to advance financially and professionally. 90% of our Franchisees started as delivery drivers and worked their way up to own one or more locations.  If you have ever thought about going to college or technical school, consider this and education that pays. A typical trainee can learn our systems and be running their own store within a year.

In your first year as a manager, you can be earning up to $85,000 a year. Doesn’t this sound like training that would be worth your time investment? After one year of being a General Manager, you can go and franchise on your own.  Not interested in Franchising, no problem! We have other advancement opportunities like Training Implementation Specialists, District Managers, Operations Directors, and Marketing Directors. All these positions need to be filled from within our company. We do not hire external people for these positions.

We currently have 21 locations in between Bloomington Indiana, and Louisville Kentucky Locations. We intend on rapid growth by acquisitions and new builds. We have an extremely aggressive bonus plan for managers that would like to take on the challenge of a new location. The last General Manager that achieved our goal earned over $32,000 bonus and is now a District Manager.

You might be asking yourself “How does the training work and pay work?”. Let us explain. This is progressive pay and training. Like we said before, we like to promote within the company and keep reading until the end. We believe like many Franchisees before, starting as a delivery driver and learning the bread and butter of our company. If you want to be successful in our business this is where it starts and with a better understanding of what every team member in the company goes through at each stage, this will make you an effective leader. After delivering pizzas and getting a feel for the business, it is time to get you slinging some pizzas. This takes a lot of practice, but this is a great time to learn how operations work from within the store. Once you become a certified pizza maker you begin management training. We have 3 levels to go through and once completed you are eligible to run your own store. The timeline depends on you and your availability. Long story short, you will go through every stage of pay per level starting as a driver to a Level 3 Assistant Manager that earns bonuses.  We are confident that you will earn a minimum of $52,000 within the first year with tips, mileage, wage, and bonuses. (working 45-50 hours a week). This is not bad that we pay you for this education. Most people don’t make this straight out of college.

Our highest paid manager earned over $145,000 last year. He also began as a pizza delivery driver. Pretty cool right? Now if you are interested in this opportunity, please understand there is no shortcuts in training. Most of what you learn is through experience. We are confident if you come with an all-in attitude, you will make plenty of money, work with cool people and give yourself plenty of doors in the future. This is not for everyone but if you apply, answer your phone. Opportunity is calling.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Chamberlain College of Nursing has immediate need for qualified Pediatric Clinical Faculty (part-time) in our Bachelors of Science in Nursing program.

Family-Centered care of children is the focus of this course, exploring issues of normal childcare as well as health alterations of children from infancy through adolescence.
