jobs.title: Legal Operations and Contracts Specialist
jobs.description:
Who We Are
Nomi Health is rebuilding healthcare with services and technology solutions designed to make access to quality, affordable care simpler and more direct. We connect buyers, providers, and patients through an operating model focused on reducing complexity, improving transparency, and removing unnecessary cost from the healthcare system.
The Impact You’ll Make
We're hiring an early-career Legal Operations and Contracts Specialist to help keep our legal function running smoothly. You'll support the Director of Legal across contract intake, NDAs, contract systems, Deal Desk operations, corporate records, and subpoena response. You'll work with our CEO, COO, and in-house and outside counsel, and you'll get hands-on training and steadily growing responsibility, including first-pass contract review with guidance from counsel.
This is a strong launch point for a career in legal operations, contracts, or in-house legal. If you're curious, organized, and hungry to learn, we want to hear from you.
What You’ll Do
Contract Intake, Triage, and Review
Help the Director of Legal build and run our contracting process.
Triage incoming legal and contracting requests, prioritize them, and route them to the right person. Learn when and to whom to escalate.
Own our standard NDA process: requests, execution, and tracking.
Learn to perform first-pass redlines on data sharing agreements, non-standard NDAs, and master agreements against our templates and positions, with guidance and review from counsel. Summarize key deviations and open issues.
Support agreements for acquiring data from data providers and other vendors.
Maintain and periodically review our templates for NDAs, order forms, and other client agreements.
Contract Systems and Repository
Serve as day-to-day administrator for Ironclad (workflows, templates, permissions, user support, and migration of legacy contracts). Training is provided.
Manage DocuSign envelopes, templates, routing, and tracking to completion.
Maintain an organized contract repository covering executed order forms, data sharing agreements, NDAs, go-lives, and terminations.
Manage the internal sign-off process and help ensure adherence to company policies.
Assist with documenting independent contractors.
Order Forms and Deal Desk
Create and maintain standard order forms aligned with current pricing and policy.
Manage the Deal Desk inbox, including partner and direct-client requests, new-client processing, and change requests.
Create and update accounts, opportunities, and CPQ quotes in Salesforce, and make sure required fields and contract execution dates are accurate.
Follow up on outstanding or unsigned order forms.
Audits and Data Quality
Perform the weekly Deal Desk audit and recurring monthly Salesforce data-quality audits (lead source and influence source reviews, unknown-account cases, debooking and termination reviews).
Support projects to streamline contract databases and account information across our CRM and finance systems.
Policy Process
Partner with team members on creating, reviewing, and maintaining internal policies.
Assist with review cadence, policy storage, and version control.
Legal and Executive Support
Partner with the CEO, COO, and counsel on document production, reviews, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinate administrative tasks for contracts under negotiation and help clarify contract terms.
Answer internal and external questions about contract terms.
Handle sensitive and confidential matters with discretion.
Corporate Filings and Records
Maintain corporate filings and records, track entities and filing deadlines, and update entity filings as needed.
Subpoena and Records Request Response
Receive and respond to subpoenas and records requests, coordinate with internal teams to locate records, and track every request.
 
 
What We’re Looking For
Required
1–3 years of experience in a legal, paralegal, contracts, compliance, or operations role. Internships, law firm or in-house legal experience, or equivalent experience count.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to stay organized across many concurrent requests.
Good judgment and the instinct to ask for help or escalate when something doesn't look right.
Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to build good working relationships.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the ability to learn new systems quickly.
Ability to adapt, pivot between priorities, and wear multiple hats.
A curious, teachable mindset and a real desire to learn and expand your role.
Nice to Have
Exposure to NDAs, data sharing or data use agreements, or basic commercial contracts.
Familiarity with Ironclad or another CLM platform, DocuSign, or Salesforce (CPQ in particular).
Interest in healthcare, data, or SaaS businesses.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent paralegal experience. A paralegal certification is not required.
Why Join Us
Hands-on mentorship from the Director of Legal and exposure to our CEO, COO, and outside counsel.
Broad exposure across contracts, data licensing, privacy, and corporate governance in healthcare, finance, and technology.
A clear path to grow into more responsibility as your skills develop.
Fully remote work with a ~250-person company.
Equal Opportunity
Nomi Health is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a workplace where qualified applicants and team members are considered for opportunities without regard to legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Mechanical Designer: Junior & Senior Level Openings
jobs.description:
Maybell Quantum is redefining the future of computing. As a venture-backed quantum hardware innovator experiencing rapid growth, we're building technology that will transform industries for decades to come. Quantum computers will be as transformative to the next 30 years as the internet was to the last 30—and our team is creating the hardware foundation to make this revolution possible.

Maybell Quantum is seeking Junior and Senior Mechanical Designers / CAD Specialists to develop accurate 3D models, detailed assemblies, and production-ready manufacturing drawings for precision mechanical hardware. This is a hands-on CAD design and drafting role. You'll translate concepts, sketches, and engineer-provided requirements into clear, manufacturable documentation, working closely with engineers, technicians, manufacturing, and suppliers.

Key responsibilities

• Create, revise, and maintain detailed 3D part models, complex assemblies, and 2D production drawings from sketches, specifications, prototypes, and engineering direction.

• Produce complete, fabrication-ready drawings with appropriate dimensions, tolerances, notes, and GD&T in accordance with applicable drafting standards (including ASME Y14.5 / Y14.100).

• Apply practical knowledge of machining, sheet metal, welding, brazing, and other manufacturing processes to improve part and drawing manufacturability.

• Develop assembly models and documentation that support reliable fit, straightforward assembly, and repeatable production.

• Create and maintain bills of materials (BOMs), part numbers, CAD files, drawing packages, and revision records.

• Perform interference checks, dimensional reviews, and routine tolerance stack-ups; work with engineers to resolve more complex fit or tolerance issues.

• Prepare CAD and drawing packages for prototypes, suppliers, and in-house fabrication; update designs and documentation based on build feedback.

• Implement approved design changes and engineering change requests/orders (ECRs/ECOs), ensuring released drawings and files remain accurate.

• Partner with machinists, technicians, manufacturing personnel, and vendors to troubleshoot fabrication and assembly issues.

• Collaborate with mechanical engineers and physicists to translate new product concepts into detailed CAD models and practical manufacturing drawings.

• Maintain organized CAD standards, templates, shared part libraries, and documentation practices.

Required qualifications

• 3+ years of professional, hands-on mechanical CAD design and drafting experience, ideally producing parts and assemblies for physical manufacturing.

• Demonstrated ability to independently create accurate parametric 3D models, assemblies, and complete 2D fabrication drawings.

• Strong proficiency with at least one parametric mechanical CAD platform (such as Onshape, SolidWorks, Creo, Inventor, Fusion 360, or NX).

• Working command of mechanical drafting conventions, GD&T, dimensional tolerancing, and drawing interpretation.

• Practical familiarity with manufacturing methods, materials, and the information fabricators need from a drawing.

• Experience organizing assembly documentation, BOMs, drawing revisions, and released CAD data.

• Careful attention to drawing accuracy, file organization, and detail while managing multiple deliverables.

• Ability to communicate clearly with engineers, machinists, technicians, and outside fabrication partners.

Preferred qualifications

Onshape is our primary CAD platform. Prior Onshape experience is valuable, but expertise in another parametric CAD system is equally welcome; we can support the transition.

• Hands-on Onshape experience with Part Studios, assemblies, drawings, and release/version workflows.

• Experience preparing precision mechanical components, thermal hardware, vacuum equipment, or cryogenic-system drawings.

• Experience creating manufacturing drawings for machined parts, sheet metal, weldments, or brazed assemblies.

• Experience with CAD/PDM or PLM release procedures and engineering change documentation.

• Formal education in mechanical design, drafting, or mechanical engineering technology, or relevant CAD certifications. Equivalent practical experience is fully acceptable.

What we offer

• $35.00 / hr - $45.00 / hr + potential bonuses commensurate with experience and performance

• Company Equity options

• Health, dental and vision insurance

• 401(k) with company match

• Paid time off and holidays.

• Professional development, training and certification support.

Maybell Quantum is solving incredibly challenging problems at the cutting edge of physics and engineering. Don’t meet every single requirement?  We are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workforce, so if you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t aligned perfectly, we still encourage you to apply.

Maybell Quantum is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse team.

jobs.title: Principal Product Architect, Growth
jobs.description:
About Pacaso

Pacaso exists to enrich lives by making second home ownership possible and enjoyable for more people. We've reimagined the second home category — pairing a thoughtfully designed co-ownership model with simplified financials, equitable scheduling, and dedicated local property management, so owners get the joy of a true second home without the hassle.

Since launch, Pacaso has facilitated more than $1.2 billion in gross real estate transactions and service fees across 40+ destinations in the U.S., Mexico, and Europe — including Aspen, Lake Tahoe, Napa, Malibu, Palm Springs, Cabo, Paris, London, and most recently Florence, Milan, and Rome. We've raised over $300 million in cumulative equity funding, closed the largest real estate Regulation A+ offering of 2025, and reserved the Nasdaq ticker PCSO as we build toward a public listing.

Our work has been featured in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Fortune, Forbes, CNBC, Bloomberg, and others.

Recognition

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for both our culture and our category-defining work:

• No. 5, Forbes America's Best Startup Employers (2026) — our second consecutive Top 10 ranking

• Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2025)

• Winner, 2025 Inman Best of Proptech Awards — Consumer Experience & Marketplace Innovation

• Fortune & Great Place To Work Best Workplaces in Real Estate (2024)

• Best Workplace in the Bay Area™ (2023)

• LinkedIn Top Startup (2022) · Glassdoor Best Places to Work, #6 (2022)

The role

Pacaso buyers are high-net-worth individuals making a considered purchase over months, sometimes years. They move between our site, email, messaging, and our Sales team, and today each of those runs on its own tools with its own picture of the customer. We believe one personalized system that follows each customer from first interest to purchase, and keeps serving them as an owner, will shorten the path to purchase and make our growth product-led.

We're hiring a principal-level technical product IC to architect that system and own its outcome. You'll define the reference architecture: how we recognize a customer across channels, what we know about them, how the system decides what to do next, and which of those decisions AI agents can make without a person. You'll prove the design with working prototypes you build yourself with AI tooling, then lead Engineering and Data in taking it to production.

This isn't a roadmap-and-backlog PM role, and it isn't a full-time production engineering role. It sits between them. You'll make product calls with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, make architecture calls with senior engineers, and be accountable for both.

Some of this is already moving. AI agents talk to our customers today, and parts of the data and decisioning exist. None of it runs end to end on its own yet. You'll take what's there, decide what to keep, and design the system that can.

What you'll own

• The architecture of the customer system. One design for new leads, dormant leads, and stalled buyers first, then owners who add a share, so the same person is served by one system instead of separate tools for each stage. You write the architecture and the decisions behind it, and other teams build against it.

• The customer intelligence layer. Identity across channels, the event and signal model, shared memory and context, scoring, eligibility and frequency caps, and the next-best-action logic that decides what happens next.

• Agent and workflow design. Which agents exist, what each one is allowed to decide, how they hand off to each other and to Sales, and the prompts, tools, and orchestration behind them.

• Trust and reliability. Evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, cost and latency budgets, and kill switches, in place before anything reaches a customer.

• The path to autonomy. What the system decides on its own, what still needs a person, and the evidence we need before we take that person out of the loop.

• Technical direction across teams. Build-versus-buy calls, data contracts with Engineering and Data, and integration standards for the CRM, messaging, email, and the site.

• The outcome. Funnel velocity (time from first interest to high intent, and to purchase) and the measured lift in qualified actions and closed sales.

Two examples of the work:

• An AI agent engages a new lead in the channel they prefer, qualifies them, and hands them to Sales at the right moment with the context Sales needs to close.

• A customer reads an email, chats with us, and comes back to the site a week later. They get one continuous experience, because the system remembers what we've already said and done.

Who you are

• Customer-obsessed. You start from the customer's experience, not the org chart or the backlog. When you have to choose between channels, surfaces, or features, the tiebreaker is what improves that experience. Our customers value clarity and discretion, and you design for both.

• An architect who still builds. You've designed systems other teams build on, and you still prototype yourself. You're expert at getting AI to do real work through prompting, tool use, and orchestration.

• Technically deep. You can read a data model, challenge an integration design, reason about latency, cost, and failure modes, and hold your own with senior engineers on how something should be built.

• Rigorous about autonomy. You design systems to run on their own, and you know how to prove they're ready. Evals and guardrails go in before launch, not after an incident.

• Accountable for outcomes. You measure yourself on results, not tasks shipped. You've stopped your own work when the impact wasn't there, and you can tell us about it.

• Fluent in business and technical. You can frame and defend a tradeoff with Sales, Marketing, and leadership, then go deep with engineers on the build. You own the decision in both conversations.

• A multiplier. You raise the bar for how Product, Engineering, and Data build with AI, through your designs, your reviews, and the patterns you leave behind.

• A partner. Marketing and Sales are core stakeholders, and you'll co-own the buyer journey with our product owner for new-lead acquisition. When the path to impact runs through another team's area, you work with the owner to move it.

• Fast at context. You go deep on systems you didn't build and turn a lot of information into a plan quickly.

What you'll bring

We'll ask for specific evidence of each of these. If you can't point to all five, this probably isn't the right fit yet.

• Customer obsession. You take customer insights and translate them into real product features that deliver results.

• A production agentic system. You've designed and shipped an autonomous or agentic system that runs end to end with minimal human intervention. You can show us what it decides on its own and how you knew it was making the right calls before you trusted it with real customers.

• A measurable growth outcome. You've owned a growth, conversion, lifecycle, or re-engagement result. You can give us the baseline, what you changed, the lift, the time frame, and how you knew your work caused it.

• Decisioning and intelligence layers. You've designed signals, identity, scoring, context, eligibility and caps, or next-best-action logic.

• Prototype to production. You've built working prototypes yourself with AI tooling, beyond specs and slides, and taken at least one to production with engineers. You can tell us what you owned and what they owned.

• Architecture others built on. You've been the architect of a system that multiple teams built on or integrated with, and you made the core technical calls: data model, integration pattern, build versus buy.

Nice to have:

• Experience with long-consideration, high-value purchases such as real estate, luxury, or financial services.

• Experience putting AI into a human sales team's workflow, including CRM integration.

• An earlier career as a software engineer, data architect, or solutions architect.

This role isn't for you if

• You want to manage a roadmap and backlog, or execute against a defined spec.

• You want to manage a team right now. This is a principal IC role.

• You'd rather be a production software engineer full time.

• You see this as an email or campaign program, or measure success in opens, clicks, or campaigns shipped.

• Your AI experience is mostly using it to write docs and emails faster.

• You need a full team and a clean data stack before you start. Some pieces exist today and don't talk to each other yet.

How we work

We start with AI. It's one of our core values. We design processes with automation and intelligence in mind from the start, and our product team already has AI agents talking to customers.

Small team, real ownership. Product at Pacaso works closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Sales, and Marketing. If you see a problem worth solving, you're trusted to solve it. We ship weekly and demo working software, not slides.

We move fast and play the long game. We make decisions and change course quickly. "Embrace an infinite mindset" is one of our values: a quarterly number is information, not a verdict, and we'd rather send nothing than send the wrong thing.

We pick up the phone and empty the dishwasher. When async isn't enough, we get on a call. No task is beneath anyone, and we keep bureaucracy to a minimum. We're a distributed Crew.

Compensation

• Around $220,000 with equity

Why You'll Love Working Here

We invest in our Crew the way we invest in our homes — thoughtfully, generously, and with care.

• Competitive base salary and meaningful equity — every Crew member shares in what we're building

• Discretionary time off — take the rest you need, when you need it

• Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family

• Sponsored memberships to One Medical, Peloton, and WellHub for whole-person, modern healthcare

• 401(k) to help you build long-term security

• Paid parental leave for primary and secondary caregivers

• Home office stipend and a monthly internet and cell phone reimbursement to set you up for great remote work

• Quarterly team gatherings and ongoing learning and development investment

Our Commitment

Pacaso is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ability, and background — including veterans and individuals with disabilities. We believe a Crew as diverse as the owners we serve makes Pacaso stronger, and we're committed to building a workplace where every voice belongs.

Benefits eligibility may vary depending on your employment status and location. Lightmatter recruits, employs, trains, compensates, and promotes regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law.

Export Control

jobs.title: Program Manager, Local Community Impact
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Community team builds direct relationships with people who use OpenAI’s technology, helps others learn from their experiences, and brings their insights back to product and research teams. Our programs connect communities with trusted partners who help organizations adopt AI effectively. 




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Program Manager to build and run our partner network. You will turn an early program into a reliable operation: recruit and onboard partners, coordinate agreements and payments, manage external service providers, support local events and marketing, review service quality, and improve the program as we learn.

This partner network will be on the ground in communities helping people–from small businesses, non-profits, and community organizations–experience concrete benefits from our technology. They will set up useful workflows, learn OpenAI tools and become more confident, independent users.

You should be as comfortable helping a partner resolve an onboarding issue as you are designing the systems that prevent it from happening again. You will work with local operators and internal teams to make sure commitments are clear, work gets done, and the people we serve receive useful, high-quality support.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Build the partner operating model, from sourcing and selection of partners through onboarding, ongoing support, renewal and exit. Establish clear expectations, owners, timelines and escalation paths. Create a scalable operating model that supports program growth and evolving partner needs.

 - Run partner onboarding with Legal, Finance and Procurement: track agreements, required information, vendor setup, readiness and start dates so partners can begin work and receive payments through approved processes.

 - Manage partner payments, reporting and related operational processes.

 - Plan and support local workshops, deployments and events with partners. Coordinate audiences, venues, budgets, materials, staffing and follow-up while preserving local ownership.

 - Coordinate program marketing and communications with Community, Marketing and content partners. Develop clear partner guidance, route brand and messaging approvals, and help useful stories and practices reach the right audiences.

 - Build trusted relationships with local operators and the organizations they serve. Coach partners, answer questions, address service-quality concerns and set clear boundaries around access, funding and program participation.

 - Create practical systems for the partner community: intake, a shared knowledge base, service logs, regular check-ins and reusable playbooks that reduce manual work without sacrificing quality.

 - Develop and operate partner review processes with the hiring manager and relevant teams. Combine verified service delivery, beneficiary feedback and sustained product use to understand performance and improve support.

 - Collaborate with analytics and product teams to assess program impact using appropriate data and feedback.

 - Manage budgets, vendors, risks and dependencies across the program. Keep stakeholders informed, surface decisions early and bring recurring partner feedback into program and product improvements.
   
   


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU

 - 8+ years owning a complex partner, community or operational program from early design through execution at scale, with clear examples of what you personally built and improved.

 - Bring strong operational judgment and follow-through across onboarding, financial workflows, events and multiple stakeholder groups.

 - Can earn trust with small-business owners, local technical operators and community leaders, explain expectations plainly and have difficult conversations when needed.

 - Have practical familiarity with ChatGPT, Codex and AI-enabled workflows, and can work credibly with technical specialists while explaining tools to people with less technical experience.

 - Use data and qualitative feedback to distinguish meaningful outcomes from activity counts, and can improve a process without making it unnecessarily bureaucratic.

 - Write clearly, communicate risks early, work independently through ambiguity and collaborate effectively across teams.

 - Have experience creating playbooks, support systems or automation that lets a high-touch program scale.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Operating a local-services, small-business, nonprofit, fellowship, ambassador or distributed partner program.

 - Coordinating vendor onboarding, invoices, budgets or grant-like payment workflows with Finance and Legal.

 - Running hands-on workshops or community events and translating successful local practices into reusable resources.

jobs.description:
Mavericks Wanted

When was the last time you achieved the impossible? If that thought feels overwhelming, you might want to pause here, but if it sparks excitement...read on

In 2015, we pioneered a “moneyball for biotech” approach, pooling projects and promising early-stage research from academia together under one financial umbrella to reduce risk and unleash innovation. This model allows science and small teams of experts to lead the way. What You'll Do

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), RFA
jobs.description:
About RFA and Titan

RFA is a leading IT and cybersecurity partner to financial services firms: hedge funds, private equity, asset managers, and the firms that serve them. RFA is part of Titan, which is building the AI workforce for IT.

Titan has raised over $100M from General Catalyst, 8VC, and CalPERS, acquired market-leading IT firms like RFA, and put AI agents into production in large enterprises. We've automated 100K+ tickets across 800+ customers and are leading the industry in service quality. Our tech team has talent from Scale AI, CoreWeave, Vanta, Dropbox, Meta, FiveRings, TwoSigma, Amazon, Harvard, Stanford, and MIT.

Why this role, why now

AI is changing security faster than anything we've seen, and we want RFA to be the one leading it for its clients. RFA's clients answer to regulators, investors, and DDQs, and they expect their IT partner to be the most security-minded team in the room. With Titan's AI agents now working alongside RFA's engineers, we can deliver security that is faster, more thorough, and more proactive than a traditional MSP or MSSP.

We're looking for a CISO for RFA: a security leader who wants to build security for financial firms from the ground up, with AI at the center of how it's delivered.

About the role

As RFA's CISO, you own security for RFA and its clients. You lead RFA's GRC, SOC, and vCISO teams, act as the senior security advisor to client leadership, and make sure RFA itself holds up to the scrutiny of the most demanding funds. You'll report to RFA's COO and work closely with RFA's service delivery and engineering teams, and with Titan's product and engineering teams.

You own and measure success by client outcomes (incidents prevented and contained, audits and DDQs passed), growth and retention of RFA's security revenue, and an RFA that passes every client security review.

This role is remote (US).

In this role you will

 - Set RFA's security strategy and lead RFA's GRC, SOC, and vCISO teams, who report to you

 - Build and run RFA's client security offering: vCISO, managed detection and response, SOC, vulnerability management, email security, and incident response, with AI agents doing the volume and people doing the judgment

 - Be the trusted security advisor to client CFOs, COOs, and CCOs: board and investment committee updates, regulatory readiness (SEC, FINRA, Reg S-P, state privacy rules), and investor DDQs

 - Lead incident response for RFA clients, from first alert to client communication and lessons learned

 - Own RFA's own security and compliance program, including SOC 2 and the security questionnaires clients send us

 - Work with Titan's engineers to make sure the AI agents working in client environments are safe: least-privilege access, guardrails, logging, and audit trails

 - Guide RFA clients adopting Claude, ChatGPT, and Copilot on AI governance: data boundaries, connector and permission review, shadow AI discovery

 - Join sales cycles as RFA's security voice: win the client's CISO or CCO, and turn what we learn into packaged services and pricing

You might thrive in this role if you

 - Bring 10+ years in security, including leading a security function or practice as CISO, VP, or Head of Security

 - Have built or run security services at an MSP, MSSP, or security consultancy, ideally serving financial services firms

 - Know what hedge funds, PE firms, and asset managers need from security: SEC cybersecurity rules, Reg S-P, investor DDQs, and frameworks like NIST CSF, SOC 2, and ISO 27001

 - Are hands-on with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, Defender, and modern EDR, SIEM, and email security stacks

 - Are excited, not threatened, by AI agents doing security work, and have opinions on how to make them safe

 - Can explain risk to a fund COO in plain language and to an engineer in technical detail

 - Take extreme ownership and would rather build the program than inherit one

Bonus

 - CISSP, CISM, CISA, or CRISC

 - vCISO experience across multiple financial services clients

 - Experience securing LLM applications or AI governance work (e.g., ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF)

Logistics

Location: Remote (US)

Travel: Under 5%, for occasional client meetings and time with the team in NYC

jobs.title: Staff System Integration Engineer, Grid Interface
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT



Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.



Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power's leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.



We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW



The Systems Team at Heron unite the systems engineering, integration, reliability, testing, and failure analysis into a cohesive group across the design lifecycle of our products. Our goal is to be the technical conscience of the product — mastering how it works, why it works, and how it can fail — and setting new standards for architecture, integration, and validation in our industry.



As a System Integration Engineer, you will carry the system through integration milestones and own the full system end-of-line test that proves it, from first article bring-up through every release, including compliance with grid requirements.

This role owns the loop from: integration build → full system end-of-line test → failure analysis → firmware and hardware fix → firmware regression on every release → grid compliance and site commissioning.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

Integration

 - Define the integration milestones (first article build, interface freeze, release readiness) and drive resolution of schedule risk.

 - Carry the system through integration milestones: track how mature each subsystem and each release is, and what stands between today's build and a shippable one.

Full System End-of-Line Testing

 - Define the full system end-of-line test spec, with pass and fail criteria that trace back to product requirements.

 - Build and run the full system end-of-line test setups and automate the test equipment so every run is repeatable.

 - Work with the firmware team on FW regression: run it on every release, own the results, and triage failures back to firmware or hardware.

Grid Interface

 - Partner with compliance team on the grid interface requirements, build them into the validation plan, and run grid compliance regression as part of the full system test.

 - Drive firmware development for grid compliance with the firmware team.

What Makes This Role Different

This role owns the question of how ready the system really is. You build and run the full system end-of-line test yourself, you carry the system through each integration milestone, and you drive the firmware and hardware changes that close the gaps, all the way through grid compliance and site commissioning. If you want direct ownership over whether a unit or a release is proven end to end, this role is built for that.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We prioritize first principles thinking, hands-on skill, and initiative over keywords. Domain-specific experience will help determine the career level for each hire.

Must-Have Requirements

 - BS in Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience integrating and debugging complete power electronics or electromechanical systems, from first article bring-up through release.

 - Experience defining and running full system functional or end-of-line test on hardware you help build, not just handing it off.

 - Experience with firmware regression testing: running it against a release and triaging failures with the firmware team.

 - Experience automating test equipment such as power supplies, grid simulators, power analyzers, and data acquisition systems.

 - Ability to write test and regression reports that firmware engineers can act on.

 - A track record of driving firmware and hardware changes to close findings, and verifying the fix through re-test.

 - Comfort owning integration milestones and release readiness across hardware, firmware, and test.

 - Familiarity with IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, and IEC grid requirements.

Nice-to-Haves

 - Experience with site commissioning and site-level protection coordination for grid-connected equipment.

 - Experience with UL 1741 or similar grid-interface certification testing.

 - Experience with grid simulators or power hardware-in-the-loop setups.

 - Exposure to utility interconnection requirements and processes.

 - Background in inverter, converter, or solid state transformer control.



If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.



Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits. The salary for this role ranges from $160,000 to $190,000 per year

jobs.title: Laboratory Technician I - Organic Prep (Multiple Shifts) Eurofins Environment Testing Southwest, Calscience, Tustin, CA
jobs.description:
Eurofins Environmental Testing Southwest is seeking a Laboratory Technician to join our team in Tustin, CA.  This position is ideal for someone who is dependable, hardworking, detail-oriented, and motivated by the opportunity to contribute to environmental testing and protecting the environment.

Previous laboratory or science experience is not required.  We are especially interested in candidates with experience in fast paced, production oriented, or hands on work environments who take pride in doing quality work and following established procedures.

The successful candidate will be trained to perform laboratory sample preparation on water, soil and aquatic tissue samples, using established methods and procedures.  This role requires someone who can work efficiently, maintain accurate records, safely handle samples and laboratory materials, and consistently meet deadlines and quality requirements.

Laboratory Technician Responsibilities

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:

• Receive, retrieve, and prepare water, soil and aquatic tissue samples.
• Evaluate workload and prioritize samples based on holding times and due dates.
• Document sample preparation details, observations, and results accurately.
• Prepare reagents and standards for daily use.
• Maintain laboratory equipment.
• Perform routine laboratory duties while following environmental health and safety policies.
• Wash and maintain laboratory glassware as needed.
• Communicate with department managers, analytical teams, and project managers regarding job status, rush requests, sample issues, holding times, and/or other concerns.
• Work efficiently to meet turnaround times and production goals.
• Follow all laboratory SOPs, quality requirements, and company policies.
• Learn and perform new techniques and procedures as training is provided.
• Assist with other laboratory activities as needed.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for someone who:

• Is passionate about the environment and interested in contributing to environmental testing.
• Is dependable and takes pride in showing up and doing quality work.
• Has experience working in a fast paced, production oriented environment.
• Can consistently follow detailed instructions and established procedures.
• Is comfortable performing repetitive hands on work while maintaining attention to detail.
• Can work efficiently and meet deadlines without sacrificing quality.
• Is willing and able to learn new techniques and laboratory procedures.
• Works well independently and as part of a team.
• Communicates clearly and professionally.
• Is comfortable working with computers and maintaining accurate records.
• Takes safety seriously and follows workplace safety requirements.
• Is adaptable, self-motivated and has a positive attitude.

Minimum Qualifications

• High school diploma or equivalent
• Ability to work in a fast paced, hands on environment.
• Ability to stand for extended periods and perform repetitive tasks.
• Ability to lift and handle laboratory samples and materials as required.
• Ability to read, write, and communicate effectively in English.
• Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship

Previous laboratory experience or a degree in chemistry or science is not required.  Candidates with experience in fast food, food production, manufacturing, warehouse operations, production environments, or other service oriented and hands on roles are encouraged to apply.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who may not have a traditional science background but has demonstrated that they are:

• Reliable
• Hardworking
• Detail oriented
• Safety conscious
• Able to follow procedures
• Comfortable working in a fast paced environment
• Willing to learn
• A strong team player
• Passionate about environmental stewardship

Compensation range: $18 - $22 per hour depending on experience and qualifications.

Position is full-time with possible overtime and weekends as needed.

Must be able to work the following shifts in addition to the initial training schedule Monday - Friday, 9am - 6pm:

• Tuesday - Saturday; 1:00pm - 10:00pm
• Sunday - Thursday; 1:00pm - 10:00pm

Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base compensation may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base compensation of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.

We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays and vacation, personal days, and dental and vision options.

We support your development! Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity! Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

Sustainability matters to us! At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Company description: Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic and labelling is accurate.

The Eurofins network of companies is the global leader in food, environment, pharmaceutical and cosmetic product testing and in discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and agroscience contract research services. It is one of the market leaders in certain testing and laboratory services for genomics, discovery pharmacology, forensics, advanced material sciences and in the support of clinical studies, as well as having an emerging global presence in Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisations. It also has a rapidly developing presence in highly specialised and molecular clinical diagnostic testing and in-vitro diagnostic products.

In over 35 years, Eurofins has grown from one laboratory in Nantes, France to 61,000 staff across a decentralised and entrepreneurial network of ca. 900 laboratories in 61 countries. Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

In 2025, Eurofins generated total revenues of EUR 7.296 billion, and has been among the best performing stocks in Europe over the past 20 years.

Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Business Intelligence Manager
jobs.description:
The Business Intelligence Manager is responsible for designing, developing, and delivering enterprise reporting and analytics solutions that support strategic and operational decision-making across National Vision. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise, analytical problem-solving skills, and business partnership capabilities to drive actionable insights and scalable reporting solutions. This role will play a critical part in National Vision's reporting & analytical advancements to a modern Power BI-based analytics ecosystem, with an emphasis on trusted data, governed KPI definitions, and executive-ready reporting appropriate for a publicly traded, multi-unit optical retail company.

•Business Intelligence & Dashboard Development

• Experience gathering requirements and delivering end-to-end reporting solutions. (Required)
• Experience working in large, complex data environments. (Required)

Additional Skills - Includes Computer/Software Skills

• Experience in retail, optical retail, healthcare services, consumer, or other multi-unit business environments.(Preferred)

Taking Care of our People!

jobs.title: Analyst, Technical Customer Manager - Public Sector
jobs.description:
At Qualtrics, we create software the world’s best brands use to deliver exceptional frontline experiences, build high-performing teams, and design products people love. But we are more than a platform—we are the creators and stewards of the Experience Management category serving over 18K clients globally. Building a category takes grit, determination, and a disdain for convention—but most of all it requires close-knit, high-functioning teams with an unwavering dedication to serving our customers.

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Analyst, Technical Customer Manager - Public Sector

Why We Have This Role

The Technical Customer Manager plays a pivotal part in Qualtrics' success by leading the design, delivery and ongoing success of customer’s experience programs, focused on driving measurable business impact. In this role, you will partner with customers throughout their lifecycle - from program delivery and onboarding to ongoing optimization, adoption and value realization.  You will act as the primary technology trusted advisor for your portfolio, leading medium and large-scale software implementations and optimizing our technology to address individual challenges, ultimately building our customers into lifelong Qualtrics champions.

How You'll Find Success

You will find success by blending exceptional customer and project management skills with a focus on technical platform adoption, renewals, and expansion. You will lead project teams to deliver complex programs within our specific Industry Verticals and Region, ensuring your customers deepen and broaden their usage of the platform. By influencing customers to shape their feedback programs and being resourceful when facing challenges, you will drive leading indicators of success, value realization, and Net ARR growth.

How You’ll Grow

Key Responsibilities

Help Customers Grow

• Build and maintain strong customer stakeholder relationships to deeply understand the context, ambition and strategic business goals for the customers within your portfolio

• Define and execute your strategy for retaining, maturing and expanding customer accounts; including assessing customer usage and implementing new capabilities to enhance their programs

• Develop success plans aligned with customer business goals and technology roadmaps

• Monitor customer health, platform utilization and adoption metrics to identify opportunities for increased value

• Contribute to a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement to drive high quality customer outcomes

Provide Technical & Execution Expertise

• Develop and maintain technical competence on the Qualtrics platform, ensuring a deep understanding of the leading indicators of customer adoption, ACV retention and value realization

• Utilize experience and best practices in order to understand the customer and communicate effectively how the Qualtrics platform will support the delivery of value driving outcomes and enhance their program

• Lead specific project implementations for new customers to your portfolio and existing customers; including cross functional / cross team project teams consisting of Technical Services Consultants and XM Advisors, with the objective to deliver on project goals and objectives

• Conduct regular risk planning, monitoring, mitigation and reporting to stakeholders both during project delivery and account lifecycle

Demonstrate Operational Rigor

• Execute implementation and account management activities in accordance with global standard practices, ensuring rigorous account and project tracking and proactive risk and issue management

• Ensure all project and account documentation and artifacts are developed, maintained

• Stay current with product and strategic customer journey enhancements

Key Success Measures

For customer accounts within your portfolio over a 12 month period:

Customer Value

• Net ARR

• Customer adoption and maturity of customer account

• Customer satisfaction and advocacy

Successful Execution

• Billable Utilization attainment

• Time to Value for customers following delivery of new capabilities (measured by level of consumption 60 days following go-live milestone)

• Time to Deliver new capabilities for customers in your portfolio

• Rigorous scope management measured by level of Variance on Completion (VAC) of specific project deliverables

Things You'll Do

• Portfolio Leadership: Own the success of a portfolio of customer accounts, serving as the primary technology advisor throughout the customer lifecycle

• Portfolio Performance: Monitor portfolio performance using customer health, adoption, maturity and value realisation to proactively manage risk and identify growth opportunities

• Account Growth & Maturity: Define strategy to expand program adoption and maturity across our customer accounts, driving Net ARR and portfolio performance

• Strategic Project Management: Partner with customers to provide expertise leading to the alignment of project goals and timely execution

• Risk & Quality Management: Plan, monitor, and mitigate project risks while developing quality management plans aligned with business requirements

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate with internal teams to support your customer’s experience and maintain account health

jobs.title: Head of Marketing Operations
jobs.description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people and teams adopt Perplexity and Computer on their own, and our enterprise marketing programs bring in thousands more leads. We've grown this far without a marketing automation platform or a dedicated Marketing Operations team. We're ready to build both.

We're hiring our first Head of Marketing Operations. You'll choose and implement our first marketing automation platform. You'll own how every marketing and product lead is enriched, scored and routed. And you'll build the campaign operations, attribution and reporting that connect our B2B and enterprise marketing to pipeline and revenue.

You'll report to the Head of Revenue Operations and build a team. Your first direct report is a GTM Engineer, who builds our enrichment, scoring and routing systems in code. You set the definitions, strategy and priorities for that work, and the GTM Engineer is your force multiplier for delivering it.



Tech stack: Salesforce | Snowflake | dbt | Clay | Marketing automation (you'll choose it) | Reverse ETL (Hightouch or similar) | Routing and scheduling (Default, Chili Piper or similar) | Computer




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and lead the Marketing Operations team. Manage the GTM Engineer from day one, set the team's roadmap, and hire the next roles as the function grows. Stay hands-on while the team is small.

 - Select and implement our marketing automation platform. Run the evaluation across established and AI-native platforms, covering requirements, integrations, security, scale and total cost. Then lead the rollout: the data model, the Salesforce sync, lifecycle stages, program templates, permissions and the migration of our existing B2B email programs.

 - Own the lead lifecycle. Define lifecycle stages, qualification criteria, handoff SLAs and recycle rules with Marketing and Sales leadership. Make sure they are enforced the same way in the marketing automation platform and in Salesforce.

 - Own enrichment, scoring and routing. You are accountable for every lead being complete, accurately scored on fit, intent and product usage, and sent to nurture or to a BDR, AE or Account Manager within SLA. The GTM Engineer builds and runs these systems. You direct the work, supply marketing engagement signals to the scoring model, and answer to Sales and Marketing for the results.

 - Own or co-own the prospecting tools our BDRs use. Lead the implementation and evolution of these tools, which will be a combination of internally built applications and vendor solutions. Work with BDR leadership to set requirements, decide what to build and what to buy, drive adoption, and measure the impact on meetings and pipeline. The GTM Engineer delivers the internal builds and the integrations with vendor tools.

 - Stand up account-based marketing and sales as a motion. Work with Sales and Marketing leadership to select and tier target accounts by fit, intent and product usage, and set the level of investment for each tier, from one-to-one plans for strategic accounts to scaled programs for the broader list. Map the buying group at each account and roll individual engagement up to an account-level score that tells BDRs and AEs when to act. Design the coordinated plays that Marketing, BDRs and AEs run together across email, ads, events and outbound, with clear triggers, owners and follow-up SLAs. Measure the program by account: buying-group coverage, engagement, meetings, pipeline and win rate against comparable non-target accounts. The GTM Engineer builds the account scoring, signals and orchestration behind these plays.

 - Run nurture and campaign operations for B2B and enterprise marketing. Build the nurture tracks that leads enter when they aren't ready for sales, including entry and exit rules. Set up a repeatable way to build, test and launch email, webinar, event, paid and account-based programs. Keep a clean Salesforce campaign structure so every program rolls up correctly.

 - Own attribution and marketing reporting. Build the tracking and lead source model, define how we measure pipeline that marketing sourced and influenced, and own the dashboards and weekly funnel review that leadership uses. Marketing and Revenue Operations should report the same numbers.

 - Protect data quality, consent and deliverability. Own consent, preferences and suppression for B2B and enterprise marketing email under GDPR, CCPA and CAN-SPAM. Own sending-domain health and inbox placement for that email. The Growth team owns product and consumer lifecycle messaging, so agree shared rules with them on contact frequency, suppression and sending domains.

 - Partner with Growth on web conversion. Growth owns the website, sign-up flows and in-product surfaces. You own what happens to a B2B lead after capture: form field standards, tracking parameters, consent capture, and a clean handoff into the marketing automation platform and Salesforce.

 - Own the marketing technology stack and its budget. Evaluate vendors, manage renewals, add what the team needs and retire what it has outgrown.

 - Set the operating rhythm. Run intake and prioritization for marketing operations requests, document every system, and train marketers and sellers on how to use what you build.

 - Use AI to do more with a small team. Use Computer and other AI tools to automate campaign builds, data cleanup, reporting and lifecycle workflows.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first 30 days:

 - Audit how leads are captured, enriched, scored, routed and emailed today, and document the gaps.

 - Write the requirements for the marketing automation platform and start the evaluation.

 - Agree with Growth on who owns which messages, audiences and sending domains.

In your first 60 days:

 - Select the platform and start implementation with a clear rollout plan.

 - Publish agreed lifecycle stage definitions and handoff SLAs.

 - Set the GTM Engineer's priorities for enrichment, scoring and routing, and publish a baseline funnel report.

In your first 120 days:

 - Take the platform live with a reliable Salesforce sync, consent and preference management, and the first nurture programs running.

 - Have scoring and routing meet the agreed speed-to-lead SLA.

 - Deliver a first attribution model that Marketing, Sales and Finance all use.

In your first 6 months:

 - Build the team beyond the GTM Engineer, based on a hiring plan you've made the case for.

 - Show a measurable lift in lead-to-meeting and meeting-to-opportunity conversion.

 - Report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline as one trusted number in company planning.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 8+ years in marketing operations or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including 2+ years managing people.

 - Experience at a company with a large consumer user base alongside an enterprise business, coordinating with a product lifecycle or growth team.

 - You've led the selection and implementation of a marketing automation platform from scratch, or a full migration, including the Salesforce sync.

 - Deep, hands-on expertise in at least one major platform, such as HubSpot or Marketo. You can still build in it yourself.

 - You've designed, shipped and measured a lead scoring and routing model, with a lifecycle and SLAs that Sales followed.

 - You've built attribution and pipeline reporting that Sales and Finance used to make decisions.

 - Experience directing technical builders, such as GTM engineers, systems engineers or analysts. You can scope technical work, set priorities and judge the result.

 - Working knowledge of the Salesforce data model (leads, contacts, accounts, opportunities, campaigns) and enough SQL to trace a record across systems.

 - Working knowledge of consent and privacy rules (GDPR, CCPA, CAN-SPAM) and email deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, list hygiene).

 - Clear communicator. You explain systems and data to executives without jargon, and turn business requests into requirements.

 - Builder mindset. You're comfortable being the first hire in a function and creating structure where none exists.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in a hybrid product-led and sales-led motion, including product-qualified leads and mapping users to accounts.

 - Experience with a warehouse-first stack: Snowflake, dbt, reverse ETL and Clay.

 - Experience deploying AI-native marketing tools or agents in production.

 - Experience running event and webinar operations, including lead capture and follow-up.

 - Experience building a marketing operations team from the first hire.

We are an entrepreneurial business – not a traditional “ad agency.” That means we value resourcefulness and tenacity just as much as we value creativity and intelligence.

What's the role?

The Group Creative Director manages the creative direction of multiple projects/accounts, ensuring the work is always the best the agency can produce. (S)he is responsible for ensuring creative development occurs in a timely manner and the work is in line with not only the client brief but the creative standards and point of view of the agency.  (S)he presents original concepts for campaigns that run across multiple mediums directly to the agency’s leadership and clients. (S)he oversees the creative staff, playing a key role in developing our creative talent.

Essential Responsibilities You’ll Own

• Ensure the timely development and execution of multiple plans, campaigns, and projects that not only meet client objectives but are breakthrough ideas for the creative industry.

• Develop creative solutions that defend budget recommendations and measurement objectives to provide both profitable and quality work to our current and prospective clients.

• Serve as the final decision-making authority on copy, text and art for creative assignments for internal executive and external client review.

• Consistently provide leadership and motivation, conveying the vision and values of the agency to staff.

• Facilitate and promote agency initiatives and values throughout each creative opportunity.

• Execute assignments as directed in compliance with agency and client guidelines and objectives.

• Train and supervise assigned staff of writers and art directors; oversee their execution of all creative efforts to ensure they are on strategy, on budget, and on schedule.

• Collaborate with the core leadership team on all accounts and projects to ensure alignment on creative recommendations and client opportunities. Work to resolve any internal differences that could potentially lead to discord in the office.

• Maintain external professional relationships with production partners, freelance networks, agency partners and others to ensure we’re sharing the agency POV across the industry and recruiting the right talent and partners

• Participate in the creation and presentation of client pitches / new business efforts, as required.

• Possess and maintain a clear and current awareness of the competitive creative environment and work being done by other agencies.

Who are we looking for?

You are results and bottom-line oriented, yet will possess deep appreciation and sensitivity towards people, culture, and values. You are thick-skinned and persistent, but at the same time diplomatic and politically aware. You are personable, smart, passionate, and optimistic. You possess a deeply pro-active, hands-on mentality. You hold yourself accountable and take great pride in your work – just like us. We’re proudly diverse in our backgrounds, our accents, and our fiercely held personal passions. We are, in every sense of the word, independent, and not beholden to anyone else’s agenda. So are you.

What will set you up for success

• A robust background with extensive experience in a client facing, creative leadership role in an agency environment.

• Proven leadership and people management skills, having the confirmed ability to successfully lead, motivate and mentor teams of creative talent.

• Strong aptitude for providing clear creative direction, career path guidance, and timely and helpful feedback that will improve creative processes, as well as keep work on budget and schedule.

• Possess an exceptional ability to prioritize work and resources across engagements based on short- and long-term need; timelines, budgets, and work that moves at the speed of culture.

• Consistently exhibit an unwavering commitment to creativity and fresh approaches to client work.

• Demonstrate, evangelize and live the core values of the agency.

• Incorporate the passion, excitement and experience of one’s MINOR in relevant ways that inform the quality and output of agencies deliverables.

• Empathy and the ability to see clearly the perspectives and views of others are integral, as is the ability to take creative criticism and move the work forward.

• Possess and encourage high degrees of initiative, drive, energy, accountability, creativity and maturity.

• Be able to work under pressure and move with the storms of pitches, brainstorming sessions, and tight deadlines with flexible agility, a good sense of humor, and solid focus.

• Be highly motivated and well organized. Keen eyes for the details are a must.

jobs.description:

When you join one of our teams, you’ll be part of a nimble group that’s empowered to set aggressive goals and move fast to achieve them. Strategic risks are encouraged and complex problems are solved together, by passing the mic and iterating until the best solution comes to light. You won’t have to look to find growth opportunities—ready or not, they’ll find you. From retail to government to healthcare, we’re on a mission to bring humanity, connection, and empathy back to business. Join over 5,000 people across the globe who think that’s work worth doing.

Principal Technical Customer Manager - Product & Services

Why We Have This Role

The Technical Customer Manager plays a pivotal part in Qualtrics' success by leading the design, delivery and ongoing success of customer’s experience programs, focused on driving measurable business impact. In this role, you will partner with customers throughout their lifecycle - from program delivery and onboarding to ongoing optimization, adoption and value realization.  You will act as the primary technology trusted advisor for your portfolio, leading medium and large-scale software implementations and optimizing our technology to address individual challenges, ultimately building our customers into lifelong Qualtrics champions.

How You'll Find Success

You will find success by blending exceptional customer and project management skills with a focus on technical platform adoption, renewals, and expansion. You will lead project teams to deliver complex programs within our specific Industry Verticals and Region, ensuring your customers deepen and broaden their usage of the platform. By influencing customers to shape their feedback programs and being resourceful when facing challenges, you will drive leading indicators of success, value realization, and Net ARR growth.

How You’ll Grow

• Master advanced technical implementation: You will develop deep, hands-on expertise in the Qualtrics platform, evolving into a trusted technology advisor who leads medium and large-scale enterprise software implementations.

• Elevate your executive influence and consulting skills: You will build strong relationships with senior customer program owners and decision-makers, honing your ability to shape strategic feedback programs and guide large, complex organizations through business transformations.

• Develop commercial and portfolio leadership: By proactively monitoring account health and defining expansion strategies, you will move beyond standard project execution to directly drive portfolio performance, value realization, and account growth.

• Expand your cross-functional and industry footprint: You will act as the critical bridge collaborating internally with project managers, engineering, account executive and product teams, while deepening your specialized knowledge of significant industry shifts taking place in experience management.

Things You'll Do

• Portfolio Leadership: Own the success of a portfolio of customer accounts, serving as the primary technology advisor throughout the customer lifecycle

• Portfolio Performance: Monitor portfolio performance using customer health, adoption, maturity and value realisation to proactively manage risk and identify growth opportunities

• Account Growth & Maturity: Define strategy to expand program adoption and maturity across our customer accounts, driving Net ARR and portfolio performance

• Strategic Project Management: Partner with customers to provide expertise leading to the alignment of project goals and timely execution

• Risk & Quality Management: Plan, monitor, and mitigate project risks while developing quality management plans aligned with business requirements

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Collaborate with internal teams to support your customer’s experience and maintain account health

What We're Looking For On Your Resume

The ideal candidate combines technical expertise, consulting skills and a passion for helping customers transform their business through technology.

• 3+ years of experience: Successfully working with large, complex organisations to execute and advise on customer facing programs that deliver sustainable business outcomes

• Technical Aptitude: High interest in learning the Qualtrics platform and new technologies and deployment of technical expertise with customers at scale

• Consulting & Program Management: Proven ability to plan and execute multiple concurrent projects on time and budget, with a blend of consulting and internal-customer experience. Collaborating with project managers, consultants, architects and product teams to support delivery of specific outcomes

• Customer Engagement: Ability to lead workshops, knowledge transfer sessions, utilise data and metrics to communicate understanding and produce high quality customer facing documentation

• Stakeholder Influence: Ability to build relationships with senior customer program owners and decision makers

• Industry Experience: Good understanding of significant industry shifts taking place in experience management in one or more specific industries.

• Entrepreneurial spirit: High tolerance for ambiguity and complexity. Ability to be efficient with limited resources, to understand business needs and to communicate and present to Senior Management effectively.

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in science, technology, engineering, or business-related field.

• Willingness to Travel: Able to travel up to 25% to engage with clients and teams.

Key Responsibilities

Help Customers Grow

• Build and maintain strong customer stakeholder relationships to deeply understand the context, ambition and strategic business goals for the customers within your portfolio Define and execute your strategy for retaining, maturing and expanding customer accounts; including assessing customer usage and implementing new capabilities to enhance their programs Develop success plans aligned with customer business goals and technology roadmaps Monitor customer health, platform utilisation and adoption metrics to identify opportunities for increased value Contribute to a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement to drive high quality customer outcomes

jobs.title: GTM Systems Manager
jobs.description:
About the Role

Navan is seeking a GTM Systems Manager to own and improve the operational systems and workflows that support our global go-to-market teams. You’ll ensure that leads reach the right teams, sellers have the right accounts, and business processes work reliably across Salesforce and our connected GTM tools.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who enjoys investigating complex problems, configuring workflows, and owning execution from request through resolution. You’ll combine deep operational Salesforce expertise with practical experience in routing, territory administration, tool management, and automation.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Marketing Operations, Revenue Operations Business Partners, Data Quality, Analytics, and Business Systems. Our Data Quality team leads data standards, enrichment, and territory data design; you’ll focus on the operational workflows that put approved data and business rules into action. You’ll work with Business Systems on Salesforce platform configuration and development.

What You’ll Do:

• Own routing operations. Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot lead, contact, and account routing in LeanData and connected systems. Translate approved business requirements into tested workflows, monitor results, and resolve exceptions.

• Run account assignment and pairing workflows. Manage recurring SDR–AE pairings, new-hire book assignments, and operational changes associated with promotions, transfers, and departures. Apply approved territory rules and validate that changes reach the right records and users.

• Manage assigned GTM tools. Own day-to-day configuration, workflow maintenance, troubleshooting, vendor coordination, and operational documentation. Keep tools aligned with changing business needs and coordinate dependencies with other system owners.

• Investigate issues across systems. Use Salesforce reports, record history, routing logs, and SQL to trace unexpected behavior. Distinguish workflow, configuration, integration, and underlying data issues, then drive resolution with the appropriate partners.

• Own operational requests through completion. Clarify requirements, prioritize by business impact, communicate progress, manage escalations, and verify outcomes with requesters. Turn recurring requests into consistent, documented processes.

• Manage account lifecycle workflows. Coordinate approved account creation, ownership transitions, stale opportunity processes, and account or user obfuscation requests. Follow established policies and work with Data Quality and Business Systems where changes affect shared records or reporting.

• Deliver reliable changes. Document requirements and acceptance criteria, assess downstream dependencies, coordinate testing and release timing, and validate production results.

• Improve efficiency through automation. Simplify recurring operational work using native tool capabilities, low-code automation, and AI-assisted tools. Partner with GTM Engineering on solutions requiring deeper development.

• Build operational visibility and coverage. Track request turnaround, routing exceptions, workflow failures, and recurring incidents. Maintain clear runbooks and handoffs so critical processes can be supported by others.

What We’re Looking For:

• 5+ years of experience in GTM Systems, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Marketing Operations, or a related function, with hands-on ownership of business systems and workflows.

• Deep operational Salesforce expertise, including object relationships, ownership, lead conversion, reporting, and the effects of automation on business processes. You can investigate unexpected behavior and translate findings into clear requirements for technical partners.

• Hands-on experience configuring and maintaining routing or assignment workflows in LeanData or a comparable platform.

• Experience managing GTM tools and troubleshooting how data and actions move between connected systems.

• Experience executing recurring account assignments, territory changes, or similar operational processes with strong validation and attention to downstream effects.

• Working proficiency in SQL and strong spreadsheet skills, sufficient to investigate discrepancies, identify affected records, and validate operational changes independently.

• Strong judgment in ambiguous situations: you establish the facts, identify dependencies, clarify ownership, and make practical recommendations.

• Demonstrated ownership of cross-functional work, including requirements gathering, testing, documentation, stakeholder communication, and delivery.

• A track record of improving repetitive processes while maintaining dependable day-to-day operations.

• Direct experience with LeanData, Salesforce-connected sales tools, and ticketing systems such as Jira.

• Familiarity with enrichment platforms such as Clay, ZoomInfo, or Lusha and how their outputs affect downstream workflows.

• Experience with Snowflake, APIs, low-code automation, or scripting in Python or JavaScript.

• Experience supporting global teams across both product-led and sales-led go-to-market motions.

• Practical experience using AI-assisted tools to improve operational workflows.

Salesforce administrator certification is not required. We value demonstrated ability to operate, troubleshoot, and improve Salesforce-connected business processes.

The posted pay range represents the anticipated low and high end of the compensation for this position and is subject to change based on business need. To determine a successful candidate’s starting pay, we carefully consider a variety of factors, including primary work location, an evaluation of the candidate’s skills and experience, market demands, and internal parity.

For roles with on-target-earnings (OTE), the pay range includes both base salary and target incentive compensation. Target incentive compensation for some roles may include a ramping draw period. Compensation is higher for those who exceed targets. Candidates may receive more information from the recruiter.

Pay Range

$105,000—$180,000 USD

Human oversight: Metaview does not automatically reject candidates or make final hiring decisions. Our recruiters and hiring managers review all outputs and make the final hiring decision regarding every application.
